title: Nigerian woman in Massachusetts charged after alleged illegal voting in federal elections
summary: Gladys Adaeze Okafor allegedly falsified her citizenship on United States voter registration cards in Massachusetts to illegally cast ballots.
story: Homeland Security Investigations agents execute a major Texas voter fraud crackdown, arresting seven non-citizens in North Texas for illegal voting. U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould pledges to prosecute individuals who lie to the federal government about their citizenship status to cast ballots. The arrests come amid a broader federal push to secure voter rolls and investigate fraudulent registrations ahead of federal elections.
A Nigerian woman living in the United States as a permanent resident in Massachusetts illegally voted in at least two elections after lying about her citizenship, authorities said.

Gladys Adaeze Okafor, 56, has been charged by the Justice Department with unlawfully voting as an alien for allegedly casting ballots in the 2024 presidential primary election and the 2022 midterm elections despite not being a U.S. citizen.
She is expected to appear in a Boston federal courtroom on Wednesday.
CANADIAN NONCITIZEN ACCUSED OF ILLEGALLY VOTING IN FEDERAL AND STATE ELECTIONS

Gladys Adaeze Okafor, 56, is charged with illegally voting in elections despite not being a United States citizen. Okafor, a Nigerian citizen, lives in Massachusetts as a permanent resident, authorities said. (Getty Images; Justice Department)
Okafor repeatedly falsified her citizenship status on official documents under penalty of perjury to gain access to the ballot, federal prosecutors allege.
In July 2022, she submitted a voter registration card and signed her name certifying that she was a U.S. citizen, authorities said. The City of Lynn subsequently registered her to vote.
NONCITIZEN CHARGED WITH VOTING IN MINNESOTA 2024 ELECTION AFTER ADMITTING ‘MISTAKE’ TO INVESTIGATORS

In October 2023, Okafor submitted another voter registration card where she checked a box saying she was an American citizen, prosecutors said. She then voted in the 2024 presidential primary election, court documents state.
Okafor was born in Nigeria and obtained lawful permanent resident status in December 2022. However, she is not a U.S. citizen and has not applied for U.S. citizenship, prosecutors said.
She faces up to a year in prison and up to $10,000 in fines.

Recently, seven noncitizens were indicted in connection with an election integrity investigation in Texas. Earlier this month, the DOJ charged five people in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Wisconsin in cases involving alleged illegal voting or fraudulent registration during the 2022 or 2024 elections.
Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

title: Taxpayer funds meant for LA homeless allegedly spent on Tahiti trip, nightclub, luxury cars: feds
summary: Three defendants face federal charges in a Los Angeles homeless services fraud crackdown involving alleged wire fraud, bribery and money laundering.
story: Federal officials announced charges against three defendants accused of exploiting programs intended to provide housing and services to homeless Californians, with two arrested Wednesday morning.

Taxpayer dollars intended to put roofs over the heads of Los Angeles’ homeless allegedly paid instead for a Tahiti vacation, a high-end nightclub, luxury vehicles and other personal expenses, federal authorities said Wednesday as agents fanned out across the city in an early-morning fraud crackdown.

At the center of the crackdown is Michael Young, 46, a founder of Culver City-based nonprofit Home At Last, who received more than $118 million in public funds through government contracts, including more than $75 million from the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority, according to the Justice Department.
Prosecutors allege Young misappropriated millions, including more than $7.5 million through a sham vendor scheme.
"The days of these wire fraud experts flying on private jets, driving around Beverly Hills in Range Rovers and doing lavish things is over," HUD Secretary Scott Turner said.
WHAT TO KNOW ABOUT THE NEWSOM-LINKED CHARITIES REPORTEDLY CAUGHT IN DOJ’S SIGHTS
Michael Young, 46, Lakiya Malone, 48, and Donye Mitchell, 55, were charged in the federal fraud crackdown, authorities said Wednesday. (Department of Justice)

Young was one of three defendants charged Wednesday in separate federal cases targeting alleged fraud and corruption involving money intended to house and provide services to homeless Californians. Two were arrested Wednesday, while a third was considered a fugitive.
FBI agents take positions outside the home of Lakiya Malone, who was charged with fraud involving federal homelessness aid programs, in Los Angeles Wednesday, Sept. 16, 2026. (AP Photo/Jae C. Hong)

Prosecutors allege Young used shell companies and fraudulent billing practices to divert taxpayer money, spending more than $1 million to open and operate Six Seven Five Lounge, a high-end Inglewood restaurant and nightclub.
At Wednesday’s news conference, federal officials also accused Young of spending nearly $50,000 on a luxury Tahiti vacation and $140,000 restoring a vintage Chevrolet Impala.
FBI agents take positions outside the home of Lakiya Malone, who was charged with fraud involving federal homelessness aid programs, in Los Angeles Wednesday, Sept. 16, 2026. (AP Photo/Jae C. Hong)
"The taxpayers did not sign up to fund this nightclub," Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald said.
WHITE HOUSE LAUNCHES INTERACTIVE MAP TRACKING BILLIONS IN SUSPECTED FRAUD

Authorities also arrested Lakiya Malone, 48, an employee of Special Service for Groups, on a 21-count indictment alleging she accepted more than $180,000 in bribes and kickbacks from Alexander Soofer, executive director of nonprofit Abundant Blessings.

Lakiya Malone, charged with fraud involving federal homelessness aid programs, walks out of her home toward federal authorities with her hands raised in Los Angeles Wednesday, Sept. 16, 2026. (AP Photo/Jae C. Hong)

In exchange, Malone allegedly provided priority referrals, including "ghost" homeless participants who never lived at the housing sites. Prosecutors allege their files were fabricated using fake welcome letters, forged sign-in sheets and falsified eligibility forms.

Soofer, who was previously charged, has agreed to plead guilty to wire fraud and money laundering. He admitted obtaining $23 million in public money intended to combat homelessness and pocketing at least $2 million for himself and unrelated businesses.
FBI agents stand outside the home of Lakiya Malone, who was charged with fraud involving federal homelessness aid programs, in Los Angeles Wednesday, Sept. 16, 2026. (AP Photo/Jae C. Hong)

A third defendant, Donye Mitchell, 55, CEO of The Big Blue Umbrella, is considered a fugitive. Prosecutors allege he obtained more than $1.2 million in grant funding after making false representations and later used grant money for personal expenses including bail-bond costs, credit card debt, family transfers and PlayStation charges.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"If you or someone you know has defrauded money allocated for the homeless, I suggest you report it to law enforcement," First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli said. "If you don’t, your door may be the next one we’re hitting."

title: Lindsay Clancy prosecutors face dilemma: Retrial or plea deal in case involving 3 strangled children
summary: Lindsay Clancy's defense attorney says he'd accept a bench trial on reduced charges, but prosecutors face pressure to retry the hung jury case.
story: Fox News contributor and constitutional legal scholar Jonathan Turley breaks down recent statements from jurors in Lindsay Clancy's mistrial and predicts where the case is headed next.

Prosecutors pursuing a second trial against Lindsay Clancy could face the same obstacle that produced a hung jury the first time: finding 12 Massachusetts jurors willing to unanimously reject her insanity defense.

Jonathan Turley, a Fox News contributor and professor at The George Washington University Law School, said the prosecution must weigh the possibility of another deadlocked trial against the political and emotional consequences of abandoning the case.

"The question is whether they could ever get a jury, particularly in Massachusetts, that would unanimously vote against this defendant," Turley told Fox News Digital. "For prosecutors, they have to weigh that, but they may find the alternative equally unappealing — to simply walk away and say, 'There are three dead children here, but we just don't think we could ever win this case.'"
LINDSAY CLANCY ATTORNEY KEVIN REDDINGTON SIGNALS HE'S OPEN TO A DEAL, HOPES DA WILL 'REVISIT' CASE
Defendant Lindsay Clancy watches jurors enter the courtroom during her murder trial on Friday, Sept. 4, 2026, in Plymouth, Mass. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via AP, Pool)

Neama Rahmani, a former federal prosecutor, said he believes the district attorney's office should try and negotiate a deal — but also that it appears unlikely due to the nature of the crime and the defense's position after deadlocked jurors split 11-1, with only a single holdout in favor of finding Clancy guilty of murder in the strangling deaths of her three young children — Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months.

"The reason I don't think there's any deal to be made here is Reddington has come out during his media tour and said that he's not going to accept any deal that results in jail time," he told Fox News Digital. "Even if you're talking about first-degree or second-degree murder, in Massachusetts, first-degree, of course, has no possibility of parole. Second-degree has the possibility of a parole. That's not something that Reddington and the defense are going to accept."
Lindsay Clancy's defense lawyer, Kevin J. Reddington, addresses the media outside of Plymouth Superior Court, Aug. 26, 2026. (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)
LINDSAY CLANCY'S LAWYER REVEALS POST-MISTRIAL STRATEGY AS RETRIAL LOOMS
The defense does not dispute that Clancy, a 36-year-old former delivery room nurse, choked her three children to death with exercise bands in January 2023. Then she tried to kill herself.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X
She survived a fall from a second-story window and is now paralyzed.
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS
Callan, left, Dawson and Cora Clancy. The three children were killed at their Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in January 2023. (Lindsay Marie Clancy/Facebook)
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE
Her defense attorney, Kevin Reddington, has argued that she is not criminally responsible for the deaths due to mental illness or defect.
LINDSAY CLANCY'S ATTORNEY ASKS JUDGE TO ACQUIT HER OUTRIGHT, ENDING CASE AND BARRING A RETRIAL

Still, he's said in recent interviews that he is open to talking about a deal, and he told Fox News' Bryan Llenas last week that if prosecutors reduced the top charge to second-degree murder, he would opt for a bench trial — one without jurors — in the hope that she receives probation as punishment.
GOT A TIP?

"I would like to see [Plymouth County District Attorney Tim Cruz] reduce it to a second-degree so we could possibly waive a jury and try the case before a judge," he said. "I would see Tim determine that the case should not go forward and dismiss it, or in the alternative fashion, something where Lindsay gets the mental, physical help that she needs rather than criminal prosecution — because I would not ever, ever in a million years have that woman go to Framingham State Prison."
District Attorney Timothy Cruz leaves Plymouth Superior Court, Plymouth, Mass., Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026. (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

As prosecutors weigh a potential retrial, Judge William Sullivan is protecting the names of jurors in her mistrial, ordering their identities to be impounded indefinitely and the confidential juror questionnaires to be impounded for at least the next 10 days.
JUROR ON LINDSAY CLANCY TRIAL SAYS 'WE LET DOWN LINDSAY' FOLLOWING MISTRIAL
Defendant Lindsay Clancy listens during her murder trial at Plymouth Superior Court in Plymouth, Mass., on July 30, 2026. (CJ Gunther/The Boston Herald via AP, Pool)

He cited threats and concerns for their safety.

title: Fellow vet remembers late Army paratrooper who helped Fox News reporter, Afghans and Helene victims: 'Send me'
summary: Army veteran Sean Michael Lee served with the 82nd Airborne Division and later helped evacuate allies from Afghanistan and set up aid stations in Poland.
story: Steven Rozina, deputy COO of the Independence Fund, honors the life and legacy of the late Sean Michael Lee. An Army paratrooper who served in Iraq and Afghanistan, Lee continued helping others long after leaving the military.
Sean Michael Lee dedicated his life to serving others.

The Army veteran with more than 20 years of military experience spanning multiple deployments and companies — including as a paratrooper for the vaunted 82nd Airborne Division — did not retire his commitment to help others when he finished his military career.
"His entire life was in service to others. Up until the very end, Sean was always thinking of others," Steven Rozina told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview.

Rozina, now the deputy chief operating officer for the nonprofit Independence Fund, which helps provide services and support to wounded veterans, met Lee when he too joined the nonprofit to continue his career of service.
ARMY VETERAN PARATROOPER WHO DEPLOYED TO IRAQ, AFGHANISTAN BEFORE HELPING RESCUE FOX NEWS REPORTER DEAD AT 50
Sean Michael Lee in Iraq. (Fox News)
"He immediately took me under his wing as somebody to teach you how to help others," Rozina told Fox News Digital.
Rozina outlined Lee’s impressive post-military resume, which spanned three continents, in his efforts to continue helping people.

"I think it was 2021, the fall of Afghanistan. Sean answered that call again. He helped evacuate thousands of our Afghan allies, people that worked with us, people that are our friends, that are still our friends today," Rozina explained.
MCCHRYSTAL, BRIDGELAND: WANT TO STRENGTHEN AMERICA? REQUIRE A YEAR OF NATIONAL SERVICE

"He got done with that mission and Sean answered the call again. When Russia invaded Ukraine, he went to Poland," Rozina said. "He helped set up aid stations, helped set supply lines. And even when a Fox News reporter, Benjamin Hall, was injured and was essentially lost, Sean was that guy that helped organize the efforts to bring Benjamin home. Sean was never the guy on the front page of the paper, but he was always there."

Coordinating a rescue operation from Poland via another nonprofit group, Save Our Allies, Lee was instrumental in the efforts to bring Hall home after a Russian attack badly wounded him while he was reporting on the war near Kyiv.
AMERICA'S WOUNDED, STRUGGLING VETERANS GET BRAND-NEW HOMES BUILT BY FLORIDA TEENS

Fox News correspondent Benjamin Hall visited "The Faulkner Focus" with host Harris Faulkner at Fox News Channel Studios on March 15, 2023, in New York City, to discuss his book, "Saved: A War Reporter’s Mission to Make It Home." (Roy Rochlin/Getty Images)
In 2024, Lee again jumped into action when Hurricane Helene devastated parts of the Southeast, including his home state of North Carolina — particularly its western mountains.
"Within a few hours, Sean was in the car, and he was headed up to the mountains," Rozina told Fox News Digital.
9/11 HERO’S MEMORY PRESERVED THROUGH MASSIVE EFFORT TO ‘DO GOOD’ FOR VETS, FIRST RESPONDERS: ‘HIS LEGACY’
"I spent a lot of time with Sean up in the mountains. I got the call, and he needed me to come with him, and we slept in our cars and helped set up aid for different communities," Rozina continued.
However, Rozina explained, "when many of us went home, Sean stayed."

"Sean stayed in the mountains, he lived in tents, stayed with communities that didn't have a lot, helped rebuild family homes, helped rebuild… there was a family store that, it was the only thing that these people had, and he was there, he was always there for somebody else," Rozina explained.
AMERICA'S WOUNDED COPS FIND HOPE, HEALING AND SECOND CHANCE THROUGH OFFICERS WHO REFUSE TO LEAVE THEM BEHIND
Sean Michael Lee. (Fox News)

Lee died Tuesday as a result of cancer he developed from exposure to toxic burn pits during his time deployed in the Middle East. He was still working out how to keep helping people until the very end of his life, Rozina said.

"I have a text message from last week where he's making plans for the next mission. The next thing that he wanted to do to make sure if another hurricane hits North Carolina, how are we going to respond? If an earthquake happens, where are we gonna go and how can we be more efficient? How can we help more people?" Rozina told Fox News Digital.
VETERANS FACE SURPRISING THREAT AFTER CANCER DIAGNOSIS, STUDY REVEALS

"Sean, in his own words, was a good 'idea fairy.' Sean came up with great ideas and really it was... Sean's plans were to be prepared, always be prepared. And it was ideas on how can we be prepared for the next emergency; the next time a veteran needs us, how can [we] incorporate our veteran community into helping others? And that was his goal was really to spread who he was, that 'send me' ethos," Rozina said.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Lee's work, through the Independence Fund and through Save Our Allies, was about helping people and using his own gifts and talents to do so, Rozina explained.

When asked what he thought Sean's final message to the world would be, he said, "Any help is still help.""You might feel like you're not doing much, but doing something means a lot. So, do what you can," Rozina said of his late friend. "Do the best you can when you're doing it. And do it with a grateful heart. What Sean did: He did the best he could at everything. And those little things add up in the end. He's touched so many lives. He has blessed a lot of deserving people and I know that his memory is not going to fade."

title: Steel Across America ends its cross-country 9/11 memorial at NY Giants game
summary: Tunnel to Towers' Steel Across America tour carried a 16,900-pound South Tower beam across 38 stops before its emotional finale at MetLife Stadium.
story: The Tunnel to Towers Steel Across America tour concluded its more than 38 stops with a final appearance at Metlife Stadium for a New York Giants game this week.
The Tunnel to Towers Steel Across America tour concluded its more than 38 stops with a final appearance at MetLife Stadium for a New York Giants game this week.

The tour featured a 21-foot steel beam from the South Tower of the World Trade Center. Starting in May, the tour traveled from the East Coast across the U.S. and then went to the New York City area to mark the 25th anniversary of 9/11 before Sunday's last stop.

The 16,900-pound piece of steel – recovered from Ground Zero in the days after the attacks by first responders who rushed to the site – has since become a symbol of the nearly 3,000 civilians, firefighters, police officers, emergency workers and military personnel who died that day.
GIANTS HONOR 9/11 HEROES BEFORE EMOTIONAL SUNDAY NIGHT FOOTBALL OPENER AGAINST COWBOYS
The Tunnel to Towers Steel Across America Tour concluded at a Giants game inside Metlife Stadium in New Jersey. (Tunnel to Towers Steel Across America Tour)

"For the past four months, communities across the country have welcomed this sacred piece of American history with incredible emotion," Tunnel to Towers Chairman and CEO Frank Siller said in a press release. "Watching people stand in front of that steel, hugging it, praying over it, weeping, reminds me every single day of why we do this work."
‘THEIR SOULS ARE IN THAT STEEL’: 9/11 BEAM MAKES EMOTIONAL STOP IN INDIANAPOLIS BEFORE RETURN TO NYC
Responders work to clear rubble at Ground Zero in New York City on Oct. 8, 2001. (Ken Tregellas)

An August ceremony in Indianapolis included a color guard, a pipes and drums procession, the national anthem performed by the Voices of the Indianapolis Fire Department and an invocation from Indianapolis Fire Department Chaplain Mike Gatliff.

Indianapolis Fire Division Chief Tom Neal and Timothy Winslow, a retired major general and executive director of the Indiana War Memorial and Museum, also addressed the crowd about the connection between the city’s first responders, veterans and the legacy of 9/11.
9/11 SENT THEM TO WAR. 25 YEARS LATER, VETERANS GRAPPLE WITH WHAT FOLLOWED

"Bringing this steel to Indianapolis, and to a museum that has stood for over a century as a tribute to American sacrifice, is deeply moving," FDNY Lt. Jack Kielty, a Tunnel to Towers board member, said. "Indiana veterans and first responders understand what it means to serve."

Frank Siller, CEO of the Tunnel to Towers Foundation, stands near a piece of World Trade Center steel that was featured during the foundation's effort to honor and remember the victims of the 9/11 attacks as the 25th anniversary approaches. (Courtesy: Tunnel to Towers Foundation)

The event also highlighted Indiana’s own connection to the attacks. Nine Hoosiers died on Sept. 11, while Indianapolis Task Force One sent rescuers to Ground Zero. Six members of the team later died from illnesses linked to their work in the toxic environment, according to the Indiana War Memorial.
Scott Nokes, a Marine Corps veteran and Tunnel to Towers recipient, spoke to attendees about the significance of allowing people to see the steel in person.

"Out of the 2,977 lives that were lost, there’s over 1,000 bodies that were never recovered specifically from Ground Zero in New York," Nokes said. "Their souls are in that steel, and if you touch it, you feel it."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

On the 25th anniversary of 9/11, Frank Siller and his family honored his late brother Stephen Siller — a heroic 34-year-old husband, father and firefighter who, after hearing about the Sept. 11, 2001, terror attack, loaded himself down with gear, and traversed through the Brooklyn-Battery Tunnel on foot heading to the Twin Towers, and ultimately giving his life — by retracing the man's steps.

"This morning’s walk through the Brooklyn-Battery Tunnel was part of the conclusion of Steel Across America, a journey that began four-and-a-half months ago and carried a 21-foot, 16,900-pound World Trade Center steel beam more than 10,500 miles through nearly 40 stops across the country and back, stopping in more than 21 states," a statement from Tunnel to Towers said. "For over four months, the steel has been a gathering place for communities to remember the events of September 11th, to honor first responders and veterans, and to ensure that a new generation understands the significance of what happened 25 years ago."
Anders Hagstrom is a reporter with Fox News Digital covering national politics and major breaking news events.

title: Texas moves to shut down police department over failure to provide 'public benefit to the community'
summary: TCOLE is revoking the Trinidad Police Department's authority to employ officers after finding the agency failed to meet minimum state standards.
story: Jennifer Combs says she was arrested on a felony charge after using Facebook to collect reports about water concerns in Trinidad, Texas. A grand jury later declined to indict her. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)

The Texas Commission on Law Enforcement (TCOLE) is revoking the Trinidad Police Department's authority to appoint or continue employing licensed officers effective Friday, following months of controversy surrounding the small Texas city's police force.
In a Sept. 9 letter to Mayor Dennis Haws, TCOLE said the department "failed to meet minimum standards" and "was unable to provide evidence that the agency provides public benefit to the community."

Regulators also cited deficiencies involving basic resources, including bullet-resistant vests and secure evidence storage, and said the department lacked 18 required policies covering areas such as use of force, vehicle pursuits, professional conduct, active shooters and misconduct investigations.

At a City Council meeting Tuesday night, Interim Police Chief Cameron Beckham blamed previous management for the department's problems and disputed aspects of TCOLE's findings, arguing that many of the deficiencies had since been addressed.
GEORGIA MAYOR FIRES ENTIRE POLICE DEPARTMENT AFTER OFFICERS COMPLAIN ABOUT HIS WIFE IN DISPUTE
Police escort a Texas mother from her home after a Facebook post about Trinidad’s discolored water led to a felony arrest. (Jennifer Combs)
"Piss-poor management is what I'm just going to say," Beckham told the council.

The department has faced scrutiny since May, when Trinidad resident Jennifer Combs was arrested on a felony false alarm or report charge after posting about concerns surrounding the city's water supply.

Combs said in a May 20 Facebook post that she had been collecting residents' photos, videos and accounts of water problems in an effort to document complaints and encourage state investigators to test water at residents' homes. She spent 23 hours in jail before a Henderson County grand jury declined to indict her.

Jennifer Combs says she was arrested on a felony charge after using Facebook to collect reports about water concerns in Trinidad, Texas. A grand jury later declined to indict her. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)
Citizen journalist Winston Noles was subsequently arrested and charged with misdemeanor disorderly conduct while protesting outside City Hall. That charge was later dismissed.

Former Police Chief Charles Gregory resigned in June. Combs has since filed a federal lawsuit against the city and Gregory alleging political retaliation. Prior Fox News Digital reporting also documented that former Trinidad Municipal Judge Shellena Bivens was dismissed after throwing out Noles' charge.
TEXAS POLICE ADMIT OFFICER MADE INACCURATE FIRST AMENDMENT REMARKS AFTER PREACHER CITED AT PRIDE EVENT

Henderson County District Judge R. Scott McKee also later questioned the "accuracy, completeness, and reliability" of information Trinidad officers provided while seeking a search warrant connected to Combs' arrest.
The Texas Rangers confirmed in July that they had opened an investigation involving Trinidad but did not disclose its scope.

Haws told Fox News Digital that city leaders will meet with their attorney Friday morning to discuss their next steps. He said the meeting could involve several options rather than being focused solely on keeping the department open.
Police cruisers with the Trinidad Police Department. (Facebook/Trinidad Police Department)
At Tuesday's meeting, Haws said the early meeting time would leave the city time to pursue measures such as an injunction or appeal if advised by counsel.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"We are going to work through this process according to the law and at the direction of our attorney as we go through it," Haws said.
TCOLE's letter also states that revocation does not relieve Trinidad of continuing obligations involving personnel records, 2026 traffic-stop data and unresolved misconduct investigations.
Fox News Digital reached out to TCOLE for further comment.
Bradford Betz is a Fox News Digital breaking reporter covering crime, political issues, and much more.

title: ISIS-K militant sentenced to 20 years for supporting deadly 2021 Abbey Gate bombing
summary: Mohammed Sharifullah admitted to surveilling a route for the Abbey Gate suicide bomber during the chaotic 2021 Afghanistan withdrawal period.
story: Senior advisor to the Secretary of War Sean Parnell honors the heroes of Abbey Gate at a Pentagon ceremony five years after the deadly attack.

A man convicted of providing material support to the Islamic State terror group in connection with the deadly Abbey Gate bombing that killed 13 American service members during the Biden administration's chaotic withdrawal from Afghanistan has been sentenced to 20 years in prison.

Mohammed Sharifullah, an alleged militant with ISIS-K, a regional branch of the terrorist group, was convicted in April of a conspiracy charge in a deadly 2021 suicide bombing at the Hamid Karzai International Airport in Kabul.

During his trial, jurors deadlocked on whether any deaths at the airport "resulted from" that conspiracy. Sharifullah could have faced a possible life sentence if the jury had unanimously agreed on that point.
AFGHAN MAN CONVICTED OF CONSPIRACY IN DEADLY SUICIDE BOMBING AT KABUL AIRPORT DURING US WITHDRAWAL

Inside Abbey Gate, British and American security forces maintain order amongst the Afghan evacuees waiting to leave, in Kabul, Aug. 25, 2021. Mohammed Sharifullah, who was convicted of providing material support to the Islamic State, was sentenced to 20 years in prison in relation to the deadly Abbey Gate suicide bombing during the 2021 withdrawal of U.S. troops from Afghanistan. (Marcus Lam/Los Angeles Times/Getty Images)

More than 160 Afghans and 13 U.S. military service members were killed on Aug. 26, 2021, at the airport, where U.S. troops were conducting evacuation operations when a lone suicide bomber detonated an improvised explosive device near Abbey Gate, an entry point.
The U.S. withdrawal was completed days later as the Taliban retook control of the country.
PENTAGON CRACKS OPEN BIDEN’S BOTCHED AFGHAN WITHDRAWAL AS SWEEPING REPORT READIES ALL THE RECEIPTS

Afghans hold documents and wait outside Abbey Gate at Hamid Karzai International Airport in Kabul during the chaotic 2021 U.S. evacuation. Many Afghan Christians and allies were among those seeking rescue. (Courtesy: Oklahoma Khorasan Church)

During interviews with the FBI, Sharifullah admitted that he surveilled a possible route for the suicide bomber to the Abbey Gate during the last days of the U.S. military’s presence in Afghanistan, according to evidence presented at trial.

"ISIS-K members provided Sharifullah with a motorcycle, funds for a cell phone and a SIM card, and instructions to open an account on a particular social media platform to communicate with them during the attack operation," an affidavit cited Sharifullah as saying in an FBI interview.
NAVY VETERAN AMONG TRIO WHO ALLEGEDLY WANTED TO BEHEAD SOLDIER AND FUND ISIS DRONE ATTACKS ON AMERICANS

President Donald Trump, surrounded by family members of military service members killed in Afghanistan at the attack at Abbey Gate, speaks during an event for the signing of a proclamation honoring the fourth anniversary of the attack. (AP Photo/Alex Brandon)

"After making these preparations for the attack, Sharifullah was tasked with scouting a route near Hamid Karzai International Airport for an attacker," the affidavit said. "Sharifullah conducted surveillance on a route, specifically checking for law enforcement and American or Taliban checkpoints."
Prosecutors also presented evidence of several other ISIS-K attacks in Afghanistan in which Sharifullah admitted involvement.
TRUMP’S COUNTERTERRORISM STRATEGY SCORES BIG WINS AGAINST GLOBAL TERROR THREATS
President Donald Trump announced the capture of Sharifullah during a March 2025 address to a joint session of Congress.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Tonight, I am pleased to announce that we have just apprehended the top terrorist responsible for that atrocity. And he is right now on his way here to face the swift sword of American justice," Trump said at the time to lawmakers.
Fox News Digital has reached out to the Justice Department for comment.
Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

title: Injured Louisiana boy hailed a 'superhero' for seeking help during deadly stabbing rampage
summary: A 6-year-old Houma, Louisiana, boy fled to a neighbor's door after a mass stabbing that killed four Verret family members before passing out inside.
story: "Look, Landry said it tongue in cheek, but there's always a little bit of truth to saying something like that, tongue in cheek. If there were no concerns, it wouldn't be said

A 6-year-old boy from Houma, Louisiana, is being hailed as a "superhero" for escaping a mass stabbing that left four dead, making it to a neighbor's doorstep and passing out inside the house after suffering stab wounds that landed him in the hospital.

The suspect, Kaegan Jude Solet, 47, reportedly followed the boy to the neighbor's door, knocked him to the ground and then fled. Once the boy got into the house, he lost consciousness, according to local WWL, and the neighbor called 911.

Solet was also hospitalized for injuries that took place during the alleged mass stabbing. He was released from the hospital on Tuesday and booked on four counts of first-degree murder and one count of attempted first-degree murder, according to the Terrebonne Parish Sheriff's Office.
MAN ACCUSED IN BRUTAL MOTEL STABBING SOUGHT AS PERSON OF INTEREST IN 4 DEATHS, CHILD ATTACK

Kaegan Jude Solet, 47, was charged with four counts of first-degree murder and one count of attempted first-degree murder, according to the Terrebonne Parish Sheriff's Office. (Terrebonne Parish Sheriff's Office/Houma Police Department/Google Maps)
The boy is "stable" after suffering multiple stab wounds, his father wrote Tuesday in a Facebook post.
"Please pray for my little man as he recovers he’s so so strong and such a fighter," the father wrote. "Current status (he’s stable) thank everybody for reaching out."

"I just wanna thank everybody for the prayers I’m trying to tell everyone thank you it’s just a lot right now," the boy's father wrote on X, sharing memorials that describe her son as a "superhero" and mourn the loss of four family members, adding his son "appreciates every last one of you reaching out and helping and praying."
DAYCARE OPERATOR ARRESTED AFTER 3-YEAR-OLD WAS LEFT UNCONSCIOUS IN POOL FOR 20 MINUTES, DIED
The Terrebonne Parish Sheriff’s Office took Kaegan Jude Solet into custody after he was hospitalized for his own injuries from the alleged massacre. (Terrebonne Parish Sheriff's Office)
"I told him earlier that he has so many people behind him and praying for him and he smiled thank yall fr , god bless."
The Terrebonne Sheriff's Office captured Solet early Sunday morning after a manhunt aided by the boy and the neighbor.

"On September 12, 2026, Terrebonne Parish Sheriff’s Office Deputies responded to the 200 block of Ashland Drive, where they located a juvenile suffering from apparent stab wounds," a sheriff's office Facebook post read. "The juvenile was transported by Acadian Ambulance Service Air Med to an out-of-area hospital in critical condition.

"As Deputies continued their preliminary investigation, four deceased victims were discovered inside two nearby residences. Detectives were called in to assist, and began processing multiple scenes, gathering evidence, interviewing witnesses, and developing information surrounding the incidents. During the investigation, Detectives identified Solet as a person of interest and began an intensive effort to locate him."

There was a GoFundMe set up for the boy and his family. The crowdfunding page identified the boy's relatives Verna Mae Verdin and Letha Verret as victims who were killed in their home during the attack. That page had reached almost $60,000 of the $70,000 goal as of Wednesday morning.

"Despite his injuries, he was able to escape and get help," organizer Brandon Thiel said of the 6-year-old survivor. "He is currently in critical condition at a local hospital, where he continues to fight for his life. This devastating tragedy has left the Verret family facing an unimaginable amount of grief, uncertainty, and hardship. The loss is especially profound for Letha’s minor children, who are now having to cope with the sudden loss of their mother, grandmother, and uncle all at once."
ICE BOSTON ARRESTS BRAZILIAN ILLEGAL ALIEN WANTED FOR MURDER DAYS BEFORE GOV HEALY SIGNED PROTECT ACT
Authorities are searching for Kaegan Jude Solet, 47, after identifying him as a person of interest in a series of deadly stabbing incidents. (Terrebonne Parish Sheriff's Office)
Solet reportedly was known to the family, and the sheriff's reports shared no motive.

"Our hearts remain with the victims, their families and every member of our community who has been affected by this unimaginable tragedy," Sheriff Tim Soignet wrote in a statement posted to Facebook. "We recognize that no words can lessen the pain these families are experiencing, but we want them to know that they are not alone and that our agency remains firmly committed to pursuing justice on their behalf.

"I am incredibly proud of our personnel and supporting agencies whose immediate response and tireless work brought this investigation to this point. Our Deputies are members of this community, and they carry the weight of these tragedies alongside the families and citizens we serve."
The latest investigation is not the first time Solet’s name has surfaced in violent crime allegations.
Solet was arrested in December 2019 for allegedly stabbing a woman repeatedly and leaving her locked inside a Houma motel room, according to a police news release from the time.
Asked why Solet was no longer in custody, Terrebonne Parish Sheriff’s Office Lt. Blake Tabor said authorities were also searching for answers.
"I can’t tell you. Certainly, that’s the hot question, right? Why is he out?" Tabor said. "We’re probably just as stunned as everyone else is."
Kaegan Jude Solet, 47, was allegedly involved in a prior stabbing of an older woman in 2019. (Houma Police Department)

Tabor emphasized that the sheriff’s office has a strong working relationship with the Terrebonne Parish District Attorney’s Office but said questions remain about how Solet’s previous cases were handled.
Deputies found four people dead inside homes near Ashland Drive after responding to a critically wounded child, authorities said. (Google Maps)

"How this slipped through, I certainly don’t know, but it’s a question that probably needs to be answered," Tabor said.

Fox News Digital reached out to the district attorney’s office seeking the circumstances surrounding Solet’s release and whether he remained under any court-ordered supervision but did not immediately receive a response.

title: Florida woman allegedly drugs man she met at club, steals his nearly $100K Rolex: police
summary: Lynda Mae Crouse allegedly drugged a man she met at a South Florida club before stealing his $98,400 diamond-bedazzled Rolex Presidential watch.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A woman was arrested after allegedly meeting a man at a club in South Florida, going home with him and drugging him before stealing his nearly $100,000 Rolex watch, according to court records.

Lynda Mae Crouse, 32, is accused of using a similar scheme at least four other times in Miami-Dade County, allegedly drugging victims before making off with their valuables, according to a probable cause affidavit.

The Broward County case she is being charged for stems from an April 12 encounter at the Carousel Club in Hallandale Beach, where Crouse allegedly struck up a conversation with the man around midnight.
The two exchanged Instagram accounts and parted ways before the man later sent an Uber to Crouse's home around 1:20 a.m. to bring her to his residence, police said.
MIAMI WOMAN ALLEGEDLY LURED MAN TO LUXURY CONDO VIA INSTAGRAM, THEN ROBBED HIM WITH 2 ACCOMPLICES
A booking photo for Lynda Crouse, 32, who was charged with second-degree grand theft after allegedly drugging a man in his apartment and stealing his Rolex watch. (Broward Sheriff's Office)

Crouse and the unidentified man had several alcoholic drinks in his living room before he went into his bedroom to change clothes. While there, he suddenly began feeling "funny" and "extremely tired," according to the affidavit.

While Crouse was alone in the living room, the man said he heard a distinctive "clapping sound." When he returned, Crouse was "acting different" and abruptly announced she was going home. Within minutes of her leaving, he fell asleep.

When the man awoke several hours later still feeling strange, he remembered the sound and rushed to check his Rolex box in the living room. His gold 40 mm diamond-bedazzled Rolex Presidential was gone.
The front entrance to Hallandale Beach's Carousel Club, where police say Crouse met the man she allegedly robbed. (Google Maps)
DRINK-SPIKING DEFENSE: NEW BRACELET AIMS TO EXPOSE DRUGS WITH A DROP OF YOUR COCKTAIL
The man later provided police with an appraisal valuing the watch at $98,400. He also identified Crouse in a photo lineup, according to the affidavit.
Months later, on Friday, Sept. 11, 2026, Crouse was arrested by Seminole police and taken to Broward County Jail.
She was charged with second-degree grand theft, a felony, and released the following day after posting $2,500 bond.
A Rolex Day-Date watch, informally referred to as a "Presidential." (Zhe Ji/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
In another case investigated by City of Miami police, Crouse was accused of drugging a victim with zolpidem, a prescription sleep aid used to treat insomnia.
Unlike the Broward County victim, that person underwent toxicology testing, which confirmed the presence of zolpidem.

title: NBC reporter, pilot among the victims identified in deadly Los Angeles helicopter crash
summary: Journalist Eliana Moreno and pilot George Marciniw were identified as victims of the NBC4 helicopter crash in Los Angeles' Chatsworth neighborhood.
story: WARNING: Graphic footage—Investigators are working on the site of a helicopter crash in the Chatsworth neighborhood of Los Angeles, Cali.
Two victims of a deadly Tuesday night helicopter crash in Los Angeles have been identified as journalist Eliana Moreno and pilot George Marciniw, NBC4 Los Angeles confirmed.
Moreno and Marciniw were employees of Angel City Air, a helicopter charter company that operated NBC Los Angeles' NewsChopper4, NBC4 reported.

The pair were covering a deadly bus crash in downtown Los Angeles when the helicopter, which NBC4 confirmed belonged to the network, lost altitude and crashed, killing a third person on the ground who has yet to be identified.
ARMY IDENTIFIES 2 PILOTS KILLED IN APACHE HELICOPTER CRASH NEAR FORT HOOD DURING TRAINING EXERCISE
Eliana Moreno seen in a news helicopter. (Facebook/Eliana Moreno)
Moreno had been a stalwart of both NBC4 and Telemundo 52's aerial coverage for years, going by the moniker "Eli in the Heli."
She had worked closely with Marciniw since 2023, with the pair sharing social media photos of them working and dining together through the years.
Marciniw was, according to NBC4, a Southern California native who graduated from Burbank High School in 1974.
Eliana Moreno and George Marciniw pose together in front of NewsChopper4. (Facebook/George Marciniw)

"We are deeply saddened to share that a helicopter providing aerial news coverage for NBC4 and Telemundo 52 was involved in a fatal accident in Los Angeles on Tuesday evening. We extend our heartfelt condolences to the families, friends and colleagues of those who lost their lives," NBC4 and Telemundo 52 said in a statement.
AMAZON CARGO PLANE OVERRUNS MIAMI AIRPORT RUNWAY AND STRIKES 'MULTIPLE' VEHICLES; 5 DEAD, 5 INJURED
The chopper crashed between two buildings in Los Angeles' Chatsworth neighborhood, producing a large fireball and injuring a fourth person.
At least three people were killed when a helicopter crashed not far from a deadly bus crash in Los Angeles. (KABC)
The injured person was transported to a local hospital in unknown condition, Los Angeles Fire Department Capt. Branden Silverman told reporters.

"Our hearts are with the victims and families of tonight’s devastating Metro bus and helicopter crashes in Chatsworth, and with the entire NBC4 family," California Gov. Gavin Newsom wrote in a statement on X.
"Thank you to the first responders working tirelessly tonight," he added.
DATA SHOWS AMAZON JET’S KEY BRAKING SYSTEMS DID NOT DEPLOY DURING DEADLY MIAMI CRASH: NTSB
Eliana Moreno poses on a helipad with Los Angeles in the background. (Facebook/Eliana Moreno)
The National Transportation Safety Bureau (NTSB) and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said they will be sending investigators to the crash site on Wednesday to probe the crash's cause.

title: Charlie Kirk's family alleges UVU knew of rooftop security risk before his assassination: legal filing
summary: Charlie Kirk's family alleges Utah Valley University failed to secure rooftops and ignored warnings before the Turning Point USA founder's fatal shooting.
story: Fox News' Claudia Cowan provides details on the Kirk family's notice of claim against the state of Utah and Utah Valley University one year after his killing. 'Fox & Friends' co-hosts and Fox News contributor James Gagliano weigh in.

Charlie Kirk's family has filed a notice of claim — a precursor to a lawsuit — against Utah Valley University, the state and key individuals involved in campus leadership and security decisions, alleging that their failures led to the Turning Point USA founder's wrongful death.

"The risk of a rooftop shooter should have been especially top-of-mind given the attempted assassination of President Trump, Charlie Kirk’s close friend and political ally, by a rooftop shooter the previous year," reads the filing, signed by Kirk family attorneys Loren Washburn, Brett Parkinson and Clifford Parkinson and dated Sept. 9.

In one alleged exchange cited in the filing, Turning Point USA organizers told UVU Police Chief Jeffrey Long that UVU students had informed them of rooftop access to the Sorenson Center, a building "pretty close" to where Kirk would be speaking the day he was killed — and directly west of the Losee Center, which is where his alleged killer fired the shot from.
CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION: TIMELINE OF UTAH CAMPUS SHOOTING, TYLER ROBINSON CHARGED

Charlie Kirk speaks at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10, 2025 in Orem, Utah. Kirk, founder of Turning Point USA, was speaking at his "American Comeback Tour" when he was shot in the neck and killed. (Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune/Getty Images)
"If this is true, it would be nice to either have it controlled access or allow one of my guys to be there as well," someone at TPUSA wrote to the chief, according to the filing. "If possible."
"I got you covered," was Long's alleged reply.
JUDGE IN ACCUSED ASSASSIN TYLER ROBINSON'S CASE EXPLAINS WHY DEATH PENALTY REMAINS ON TABLE IN WRITTEN ORDER
Read the notice:

Kirk, a 31-year-old father of two, was shot and killed on Sept. 10, 2025 in the campus courtyard, and authorities say a lone gunman took a sniper's perch on the Losee Center rooftop on the far side of the clearing. Lawyers for the suspect, 23-year-old Tyler Robinson, pleaded not guilty on his behalf at an arraignment nearly a year later.

"His murder was entirely preventable and, in fact, would not have happened had the State of Utah and UVU followed through on their stated security promises, which included protecting the rooftops surrounding the quad where Charlie was speaking," said Brett Parkinson, counsel for the Kirk family. "Those failures not only robbed Charlie Kirk of his life, but also robbed his family of their husband, father, son, and brother, with impacts that will compound for the rest of their lives."

Charlie Kirk appears at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10, 2025 in Orem, Utah. Kirk, founder of Turning Point USA, was speaking at his "American Comeback Tour" when he was shot in the neck and killed. (Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune/Getty Images)

The prospective plaintiffs in the filing are Kirk's widow, Erika Kirk, and their two juvenile children. It also acknowledges potential claims from his parents, Robert and Kathryn. The filing does not specify monetary damages. In addition to the wrongful death claim, it also raises a claim of "state-created danger" under the U.S. Constitution.
UVU said it is "aware of the notice of claim," and that it "addresses legal matters consistent with our established processes."
"Our focus remains on supporting our campus community," the university said in a statement.
REMEMBERING CHARLIE KIRK: TURNING POINT USA'S ANDREW KOLVET REFLECTS ON CONSERVATIVE GROUP'S CHALLENGING YEAR

Kirk, who built TPUSA into the country's largest conservative campus and youth-oriented activist organization in the country, also spoke at the Republican National Conventions in 2016, 2020 and 2024. He had become a personal friend of the president's as well as other prominent figures, including leading Utah politicians, the notice continues.
Ladder and rooftop ledge leading to the roof of the Losee Center at Utah Valley University — with no security gate in place. (Stepheny Price/Fox News Digital)
As a result, he had detractors, faced death threats, and publicly spoke about that before his assassination.

"You should not have to walk around with security for your entire family and for myself just because you support a politician or political candidate or certain values," he said at an event in May 2025.
"We get death threats," he continued. "People want to murder us."
ERIKA KIRK URGES CONSERVATIVE STUDENTS NOT TO BACK DOWN IN FIRST SCHOOL YEAR SINCE CHARLIE'S ASSASSINATION

Political violence was on the rise as Kirk geared up for TPUSA's 2025 campus speaking events, titled, "The American Comeback Tour." The filing references the numerous attempts on Trump's life, the home invasion hammer attack on California Rep. Nancy Pelosi's husband, Paul, and the murders of former Minnesota House Speaker Melissa Hortman and her husband, Mark.

The scene after shots were fired at an appearance by Charlie Kirk at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10, 2025 in Orem, Utah. Kirk, founder of Turning Point USA, was speaking at his "American Comeback Tour" when he was shot in the neck and killed. (Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune/Getty Images)

"Tragically, the UVU Parties failed to rise to the occasion," the filing alleges. "Through a series of stunning failures and reckless decisions, the UVU Parties created a foreseeable danger to Charlie."
SURVEILLANCE VIDEO TIMELINE TRACKS ACCUSED CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSIN ACROSS UVU CAMPUS BEFORE FATAL ROOFTOP SHOT

The allegations include a failure to perform a meaningful risk assessment or understand the significance of Kirk's visit to the UVU campus. Campus police allegedly did not have a written security plan or hold a security briefing in advance.

The second was "walking [Kirk] into a fishbowl" — surrounded on all sides by tall buildings or other elevated positions. "The UVU Parties could have declined to approve the Tour event in the outdoor quad location, or could have moved the venue indoors or to a more secure location, as it had done for controversial speakers in the past," according to the filing. The school also failed to dedicate additional resources for the outdoor venue despite the allegedly greater risk.
A view of the location where Charlie Kirk was shot one year ago. (Alec Thornock for Fox News Digital)
TYLER ROBINSON HEARING ENDS WITHOUT RULING AS EVIDENCE DISMANTLES CHARLIE KIRK CONSPIRACY CLAIMS
There were only six campus police officers assigned to the event, while Kirk's appearance attracted roughly 3,000 spectators, according to the filing.

"On information and belief, [UVU Campus Police] Chief Jeffrey Long requested approval from then-UVU President, Astrid Tuminez, to allocate more than the six officers — which represented only 25% of the UVU police force — but his request was denied," the filing continues.
FRIEND OF CHARLIE KIRK LABELS COURTROOM EVIDENCE 'DEVASTATING' AFTER CHILLING SURVEILLANCE FOOTAGE SHOWN
New security measures have been added to the area where the alleged assassin shot and killed Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk. (Stepheny Price/Fox News Digital)
After the denial, campus police did not seek additional resources from neighboring departments, such as the Orem or Provo police departments, according to the filing.

"The UVU Parties’ planning was so deficient that when Mr. Kirk was shot first responders were not available and Mr. Kirk was transported to Timpanogos Regional Hospital in a private vehicle, not an ambulance," the notice continues.
CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION: EXCLUSIVE PHOTOS SHOW PATH TO CAMPUS ROOFTOP WEEKS LATER AS ACCESS SCRUTINIZED

The school and its leaders also had "exclusive power" that TPUSA and Kirk's security team did not have, such as authority to create a security perimeter, use physical barriers, deploy metal detectors or use other "common sense safety measures like those utilized at sporting events on campus."
Area near the roof of the Losee Center on the campus of Utah Valley University. (Stepheny Price/Fox News Digital)
SEND US A TIP

Although the campus had a security camera system, footage was not monitored in real time, according to the filing — and there were no drones to monitor rooftops or any other part of the "sprawling outdoor event."

"After-the-fact review of the footage at the Preliminary Hearing in the criminal prosecution of the alleged shooter Tyler Robinson showed the shooter running across the roof of the Losee Building to a 'sniper’s nest,'" attorneys for the Kirk family wrote. "If such footage had been monitored in real-time, Kirk’s tragic death could have been avoided."

An approximation of the suspected movements of Tyler Robinson, Charlie Kirk's alleged assassin, based on court documents, video from the scene and conversations with law enforcement. (Google Maps, Fox News Digital)
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Despite warnings to the police chief about rooftop access in the area, the Losee Center rooftop was not secured. This, according to the filing, happened despite the fact that students were known to frequent the rooftop and people often found discarded "beer bottles and other trash" or paraphernalia there.
Together, all the alleged failures placed Kirk's life in danger, according to the filing.

The pathway to the roof of the Losee Center at Utah Valley University remains largely unmonitored following the assassination of Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk. (Stepheny Price/Fox News Digital/Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"He was legally entitled to believe that when the UVU Parties approved the Tour event to be held on campus on September 10, that the UVU Parties would only hold the event in a venue and with associated security measures that made the event safe for him to attend and participate in," the notice reads. "Instead, Mr. Kirk was exposed to the danger of a rooftop shooter that took his life."

title: US military releases footage of massive operation to rescue injured airman stranded inside Iran
summary: Newly released video from the U.S. military shows elite Air Force pararescue operators rescuing an injured F-15E Strike Eagle crewman stranded deep inside Iran earlier this year.
story: US military unveils dramatic footage of daring Dude 44 rescue deep inside Iran (Credit: U.S. Air Forces Central).

The U.S. military released dramatic new video on Tuesday showing parts of one of the largest combat search-and-rescue operations in its history, including the moment elite Air Force pararescue operators reached a badly injured American airman stranded deep inside Iran.

The footage documents portions of the massive April operation to rescue the two-man crew of an F-15E Strike Eagle, call sign Dude 44, after the fighter was shot down by an Iranian shoulder-fired missile.
The pilot, known as Dude44 Alpha, and the backseat weapons systems officer, Dude44 Bravo, ejected from the aircraft and landed miles apart, leaving both stranded inside Iran.

While Dude44 Alpha was rescued after a little more than six hours, Dude44 Bravo suffered a broken back, arm and shoulder after a damaged parachute led to a hard landing. He remained stranded for nearly two days before U.S. forces reached him.
HOLLYWOOD LEGEND MAKING MOVIE ABOUT EPIC IRAN RESCUE MISSION TO SAVE F-15 FIGHTER JET CREW

Newly released U.S. military video shows Air Force pararescue operators reaching Dude44 Bravo on a mountain ridgeline after the injured airman spent nearly two days stranded inside Iran. (U.S. Air Forces Central)
The newly released video shows U.S. military helicopters searching for Bravo as American forces worked to locate and recover him.
Despite his injuries, Bravo moved away from his landing site and began climbing toward a roughly 7,000-foot ridgeline as daylight revealed the desert valley and steep cliffs surrounding him.
The footage also shows American bombers and drones striking Iranian Revolutionary Guard forces that were in proximity to Bravo.
TRUMP RETALIATES AFTER IRAN ATTACK AS EXPERT WARNS REGIME IS GROWING MORE DANGEROUS
U.S. military helicopters search for Dude44 Bravo during a massive combat search-and-rescue operation after his F-15E Strike Eagle was shot down over Iran in April. (U.S. Air Forces Central)
"There was clear intent out of the Iranian ground force to come find those two guys," Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman Gen. Dan Caine told CBS News this week.
The video then shows the dramatic moment on April 5 when two elite Air Force pararescue operators, known as PJs, reached the injured Bravo on the mountain ridgeline.
Two large search-and-rescue aircraft had landed on a makeshift desert runway before smaller "Little Bird" helicopters flew toward Bravo's position on the ridgeline.
Bravo called the moment he saw his rescuers "one of the greatest moments of my life."
HOW IRAN ATTACKS ARE FORCING THE PENTAGON TO RETHINK ITS DECADES-OLD MIDDLE EAST BASE STRATEGY

Newly released military footage shows U.S. bombers and drones striking Iranian Revolutionary Guard forces near Dude44 Bravo as American forces worked to rescue the stranded airman. (U.S. Air Forces Central)
"Let's go," he recalled telling them.
The second rescue operation put 92 U.S. service members on the ground in Iran, marking the first time American forces had boots on the ground in the country since 1980.

Hundreds of U.S. service members also supported the operation from the air, while between 3,000 and 5,000 service members supported the rescue mission overall, according to U.S. Central Command Commander Adm. Brad Cooper.
But the operation was not over once Bravo was reached.

The landing gear of the two rescue aircraft became trapped in the desert sand, stranding Bravo and more than 90 U.S. service members inside Iran. A clandestine Air Force unit was ultimately brought in to extract the group, CBS News reported.
Bravo was finally brought to safety roughly 50 hours after Dude 44 was shot down. The rescue was completed as the sun rose on Easter Sunday.

title: Multiple death sentences in different states are set to be carried out within 24 hours: 'Not very common'
summary: Multiple U.S. executions in the U.S. are set within 24 hours this week, part of a surge that has seen 25 death penalty cases in 2026 with more to come.
story: Death Penalty Information Center Executive Director Robin Maher said it is rare for multiple executions to be carried out in numerous states within a couple days.
Multiple executions are scheduled in the U.S. in as many states within a 24-hour window this week.

Georgia and Texas had each planned to put a man to death within an hour of each other on Wednesday before a court stepped in to halt the one in Georgia for now, while Alabama is set to carry out another execution the following day. Texas remains scheduled to execute LeJames Norman on Wednesday after a Georgia judge stayed Stacey Humphreys' execution late Tuesday.

In the Peach State, 53-year-old Humphreys was set to be executed on Wednesday for his conviction in the 2003 murders of two real estate agents, 21-year-old Lori Brown and 33-year-old Cindy Williams. But a Cobb County judge stayed his execution late Tuesday, meaning the execution cannot move forward unless the stay is lifted or overturned by a higher court.
About an hour after that execution was initially set to happen, Texas scheduled to execute Norman, 40, for the triple murder of his neighbors during a robbery that turned deadly in 2005.
GEORGIA KILLER WHO MURDERED TWO SUBURBAN REAL ESTATE AGENTS FACES EXECUTION AFTER 23-YEAR WAIT FOR JUSTICE

Jeffery Lee, LeJames Norman and Stacey Humphreys have execution dates scheduled, although Humphreys' execution has been stayed by a Georgia judge, in three different states within a 24-hour window. (Alabama Department of Corrections:Texas Department of Criminal Justice:Georgia Department of Corrections)
Then on Thursday, Alabama plans to execute Jeffery Lee, 50, for a double murder carried out during a 1998 pawn shop holdup.

"It's not very common to have this many executions just across a couple of days," Death Penalty Information Center Executive Director Robin Maher told Fox News Digital. "This month, the month of September, we have eight executions scheduled. Last year, in October, we had seven executions in a single month. But before then, we'd have to go back all the way to 2010 to see that number in a single month."

"Just earlier this year, in August, there were three executions on the same day," she continued. "This is an unusual year in that we're seeing occurrences like a number of executions scheduled on the same day or during the same month. But there's no evidence there's any coordination among the states to have all these executions occur simultaneously. This looks largely to be a coincidence."

On Aug. 13, three states — Tennessee, Oklahoma and Alabama — carried out three lethal injections on the same day, marking the first time three states executed prisoners on the same day since January 7, 2010.
Weeks earlier, on July 28, Florida carried out two executions in a single day, which was the Sunshine State's first double execution in decades.
FLORIDA EXECUTES 74-YEAR-OLD FOR WIFE'S MURDER, BECOMING OLDEST INMATE PUT TO DEATH IN STATE'S MODERN HISTORY

Texas is scheduled to execute LeJames Norman on Wednesday after a Georgia judge stayed Stacey Humphreys' execution, while Alabama is set to carry out another execution the following day. (AP Photo/Sue Ogrocki)

In 2026, 25 executions have been carried out in the U.S., and 14 are scheduled for the remainder of the year, although that number could change if courts issue stays or states schedule additional executions.
Last year, 11 states carried out 47 executions, making up the most executions carried out in a single year in the U.S. since 2009.

Leading the way in executions is Florida, which set a record with 19 inmates put to death in 2025, more than 40% of the U.S. total for the year. It also carried out 15 so far in 2026, accounting for 60% of this year's total across the country.
Across 2025 and 2026 thus far, Florida accounts for about 47% of the nation’s executions, as it continues its accelerated pace amid a flurry of death warrants signed by Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis.

Texas, Alabama and South Carolina followed Florida, with eight, six and five executions, respectively, in that window. Texas carried out five executions in 2025 and three so far in 2026, Alabama executed five people in 2025 and one in 2026 and South Carolina put five people to death — all in 2025.
In 2026, 25 executions have been carried out in the U.S., and 14 are scheduled for the remainder of the year. (The Promise of Justice Initiative via AP)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Last year was a very unusual year. It was the most executions we've seen in 15 years in the United States," Maher said. "This year, we do not expect to reach that number of executions again. There are a number of other warrants that are still open for this year, but I don't think we'll reach the high that we reached last year."

"All of this is really due to Florida," she added. "Gov. DeSantis has decided that he wants to set a record in the number of executions that are conducted during his term. He has scheduled an execution for roughly every two weeks in the state of Florida, both last year and this year."

Two executions remain scheduled in Florida for the rest of 2026. Curtis Beasley, 77, is set to be executed Sept. 29 for the 1995 murder of a woman who was bludgeoned with a hammer, while William Lee Thompson, 74, is scheduled for execution Oct. 13 for the 1976 murder of a woman who was beaten, tortured and killed with a chain-link belt.

title: 3 dead, 1 hospitalized after news helicopter crashes in Los Angeles commercial area
summary: Three people are dead, and one person is hospitalized after a news helicopter crashed between two commercial buildings in the Chatsworth area of Los Angeles, authorities said.
story: WARNING: Graphic footage—Investigators are working on the site of a helicopter crash in the Chatsworth neighborhood of Los Angeles, Cali.
Three people are dead, and one person is hospitalized after a news helicopter crashed Tuesday night in Los Angeles, authorities said.
The Los Angeles Fire Department said more than 70 firefighters responded just before 7 p.m. to the crash between two commercial buildings at 9151 N. Mason Ave. in Chatsworth.

NBC Los Angeles confirmed that the helicopter involved was its NewsChopper4. The aircraft was providing aerial coverage of a deadly crash involving a bus and an SUV in the Chatsworth area of Los Angeles when it went down.
PENNSYLVANIA STATE POLICE HELICOPTER, SMALL PLANE COLLIDE IN MIDAIR, KILLING 1 AND INJURING 2 STATE TROOPERS
Three people were pronounced dead at the scene of the helicopter crash and a fourth was transported to a local hospital in unknown condition, according to the department.

One of the victims was a pedestrian in the parking lot, according to LAFD Capt. Branden Silverman. The other two victims were aboard the helicopter and have since been identified as Angel City Air employees Eliana Moreno and George Marciniw, according to NBC4.

Moreno was an aerial photojournalist for NBC4 and its Spanish-language sister station, Telemundo 52. She joined Angel City Air’s helicopter team in 2010 after graduating from Chapman University with a degree in broadcast journalism and political science, according to the station.

title: Fourth Florida resident dies after contracting flesh-eating bacteria commonly linked to oysters
summary: Florida reports fourth Vibrio vulnificus death in 2026 as health officials warn about raw oysters, contaminated water and severe infections.
story: Fox News senior medical analyst Dr. Marc Siegel warns beachgoers about the rise of Vibrio vulnificus, a deadly flesh-eating bacterium found in warm salt waters.
Editor’s note: The headline of this story was updated for clarity.
A fourth person in Florida has died after contracting flesh-eating bacteria commonly linked to consuming raw or undercooked shellfish, including oysters, health officials said.
The death was included Thursday in the Florida Department of Health's updated fatality count for the deadly flesh-eating bacterium Vibrio vulnificus.
The individual was from Broward County and between the ages of 75 and 79, WSFA reported. It remains unclear exactly how the person contracted the infection.
Previous deaths were attributed to residents of Bay, Palm Beach and Marion counties, according to the state’s health department.
BEACHGOERS WARNED AFTER DEADLY 'FLESH-EATING' BACTERIA KILLS 5 IN SOUTHERN STATE
Florida health officials warned that eating raw or undercooked oysters can lead to infection with Vibrio vulnificus, a flesh-eating bacterium. (iStock)
"Most people get vibriosis by eating raw or undercooked shellfish, particularly oysters," the Florida Department of Health said.
According to the department's website, Florida has reported 21 cases of Vibrio vulnificus in 2026.
In the last 10 years, 2022 and 2024 reported some of the highest numbers of cases and deaths in the region. Florida recorded 19 deaths and 82 cases in 2024, while 2022 saw 17 deaths and 74 cases.
NORTH CAROLINA MOUNTAIN COMMUNITY BRACES FOR HURRICANE SEASON TWO YEARS AFTER HELENE'S BRUTAL IMPACT

Officials said the unusual increase stemmed from certain counties experiencing impacts from hurricanes Helene and Ian. Severe weather events that cause standing or floodwaters pose a risk of exposure to the bacteria, officials said.
Vibrio vulnificus is a naturally occurring bacterium found in warm, brackish seawater.
POPULAR BEACHES CLOSED AS HIGH BACTERIA LEVELS RAISE HEALTH CONCERNS FOR SWIMMERS
Vibrio vulnificus bloodstream infections are fatal about 50% of the time, according to Florida health officials. (CDC.gov)
Exposure can occur when a person eats contaminated shellfish with the bacteria or enters contaminated water with an open wound.
Health officials said bloodstream infections caused by Vibrio vulnificus are fatal about 50% of the time.
While healthy individuals typically develop a mild illness, Vibrio vulnificus infections can cause severe illness in people with weakened immune systems.

"A recent study showed that people with these pre-existing medical conditions were 80 times more likely to develop Vibrio vulnificus bloodstream infections than healthy people," Florida health officials said.
'I THOUGHT I HAD THE FLU': MOM NEARLY DIED AFTER DISMISSING DEADLY SEPSIS SYMPTOMS

In this aerial view, a person walks through floodwaters that inundated a neighborhood after Hurricane Milton came ashore in 2024, in Punta Gorda, Fla. Flooding and standing water can increase the risk of exposure to Vibrio vulnificus, health officials said. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images, File)

Severe infections can cause symptoms including fever, chills, decreased blood pressure, also known as septic shock, and blistering skin lesions. In some cases, wound infections can lead to tissue damage requiring amputation.

Elsewhere along the Gulf Coast, Louisiana has reported 15 cases and six deaths this year as of Sept. 9, according to the Louisiana Department of Health. Fourteen of the cases were attributed to wound or seawater exposure.
The Texas Department of State Health Services says Texas typically sees an average of 33 cases per year.
Mississippi reported three cases as of August, according to the state’s health department.

title: Injured climber crawls ‘through the night’ to safety after falling 500 feet down California mountain
summary: Mount Shasta rescue crews finds San Jose man in a remote cabin after a glissading accident at Shasta-Trinity National Forest.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A California climber who suffered significant injuries after falling 500 feet down Mount Shasta spent the night crawling to a remote cabin, where he was found by rescue crews the following day, forest officials said Friday.

The San Jose man, who was not identified, lost control while sliding down Avalanche Gulch, a steep, snow and ice-covered route, Thursday night after reaching the summit in the Shasta-Trinity National Forest.

"The climber told rescuers that he had attempted to glissade down the mountain, lost control, and slid approximately 500 feet. During his fall, he sustained several significant lacerations and injuries to his feet," forest service officials said.
Authorities added that the climber was unable to call for help because his cellphone died shortly after summiting.
MOUNTAIN CLIMBER SURVIVES TERRIFYING 500-FOOT FALL IN CALIFORNIA'S SIERRA NEVADA, NIGHT STRANDED ON LEDGE
The climber lost control while glissading down Avalanche Gulch and crawled through the night after removing his boots. (U.S. Forest Service / Shasta-Trinity National Forest)
Due to the painful swelling that occurred after the fall, the climber reportedly removed his boots and "crawled through the night" down the remainder of Avalanche Gulch to Horse Camp Cabin.
By the next day, his friends were unable to contact him and reported him missing to the Siskiyou County Sheriff’s Office.
Rescue teams and air support were mobilized across several agencies by 2 p.m. Friday, and began searching the Avalanche Gulch area, officials said.
Two hours later, they were alerted that the climber was inside Horse Camp Cabin after a hiker entered the cabin and found him there.
MISSOURI DEPUTY AG, MISSING 6 DAYS AFTER SEEKING TO SUMMIT WYOMING'S TALLEST PEAK, IS FOUND ALIVE
Officials praised the climber for knowing the route, notifying friends of his plans and making his way to Horse Camp Cabin. (U.S. Forest Service / Shasta-Trinity National Forest)
Officials used the incident to remind hikers to allow plenty of daylight for their hikes, establish a turnaround time around noon, carry backup electronics and be prepared to self-rescue.

"The climber did his best to self-rescue despite significant injuries, and knew his route well enough without a map, to find his way back to the Horse Camp Cabin. Never rely solely on a GPS or phone to navigate – if those devices stop working, your own navigation skills will be critical in ensuring a safe return home," officials said.
They further commended the climber for notifying his friends of his whereabouts before he went missing.

"The climber wisely notified his friends of his plan to climb Mount Shasta and made a point to check in and provide progress updates. When he lost contact, his friends contacted law enforcement to report him overdue and traveled to help with the search effort. It is always advisable to notify at least one person of your itinerary," officials said.
CLIMBER STRANDED ON 6-INCH LEDGE AT 11,000 FEET AS 46 MPH WINDS GROUND RESCUE HELICOPTER
Friends contacted authorities after the climber failed to check in, prompting a multi-agency search near Mount Shasta. (U.S. Forest Service — Shasta-Trinity National Forest)
The rescue team was assisted by the Mount Shasta Climbing Rangers, Siskiyou County Sheriff’s Search and Rescue, and a California Highway Patrol helicopter crew.
The incident marks the latest rescue operation in the Northern California forest, where rescue teams respond to numerous incidents annually.
According to the mountain’s website, the route to the summit via Avalanche Gulch is steep and rigorous, requiring proper equipment and snow-travel skills.

In late June, another 31-year-old novice climber was flown to a hospital after slipping and falling 1,500 feet.

title: Arizona man says he lost $475k home to HOA foreclosure over less than $1,000 in unpaid dues
summary: Toby Newton says his Mesa HOA refused payment arrangements on just $977 in unpaid dues, then sold his $475,000 home at auction for only $8,172.
story: Toby Newton says his home was foreclosed on after falling behind on HOA dues and that his attempts to arrange a payment plan were rejected.
An Arizona man had his $475,000 home sold from under him by his homeowners' association (HOA) after falling behind on his dues, which amounted to less than $1,000.

Toby Newton, 53, purchased the four-bedroom home in Mesa in 2022, but fell behind on his quarterly HOA dues after losing his sales job and being diagnosed with diabetes, he told Fox News Digital. In addition, his partner has been battling breast cancer, he said.

"I was a year and a half behind because of the situation I found myself in with my girlfriend and myself getting sick," Newton said. "That's how it started. I called the HOA to make an arrangement with them to get them paid and they wouldn't talk to me. They told me I had to talk to their attorney and that's when it blew up."
83-YEAR-OLD WINS SETTLEMENT AFTER HONOLULU SLAPPED HER WITH $590K FINE OVER WEBSITE GLITCH
Toby Newton's Mesa, Arizona home was sold after his HOA began foreclosure proceedings because he owned less than $1,000 in dues, he said. (Toby Newton)
Newton paid about $170 to the HOA every three months, eventually owing $977 after getting into financial trouble.
Fox News Digital has reached out to the HOA's attorney.

Newton reportedly contacted the Superstition Springs Community Master Association in an effort to work out a payment so he could catch up on his dues. Initially, he offered to pay an extra $50 per month on top of his monthly assessments in an effort to chip away at his debt.
That was denied, he said.
83-YEAR-OLD WOMAN SUES HONOLULU AFTER WEBSITE ERROR TURNED INTO $590K NIGHTMARE
A monthly increase of $200 was also rebuffed, he said. The HOA eventually began foreclosure proceedings.
"I just don't understand how an HOA that's supposed to be there for the community doesn't work with the community at all," Newton said.

Meanwhile, the debt ballooned to nearly $10,000, Newton said, mostly for attorney's fees for the HOA. The home was sold at a public auction in November 2025 for just $8,172, the Mesa Tribune reported.

"The sale happened and I'm still in the house," said Newton. "I haven't been kicked out yet. That's what I'm trying to avoid. I'm just trying to save it because I don't know how it could go from owing them $977 to $10,000."

Toby Newton sits inside the living of his Mesa, Arizona home. His homeowners association took action against him after he fell behind his quarterly dues by less than $1,000, Newton said. (Toby Newton)
Newton said he wasn't aware of the auction until two days before. He said he has no plans to leave the home, which he purchased to spend his golden years after retirement.
"We are holding on to hope that we may still have a chance to buy our home back," an online fundraiser created by Newton and his partner states.
TRUMP SCORES MAJOR WIN AS CONGRESS PASSES HOUSING CRACKDOWN ON WALL STREET INVESTORS
HOAs have long been accused of abusing their authority and fining, or even foreclosing on homeowners, for committing even the most mundane violations.

Across the country, many HOAs are taking a tougher stance on unpaid dues amid mounting financial pressures. Real estate experts have said the aggressive collection efforts are being driven by rising operating costs, shrinking reserve funds, and concerns that unpaid assessments could leave associations unable to cover essential expenses, FOX Business previously reported.

HOA-related foreclosures have jumped nearly 40% compared with two years earlier, The Wall Street Journal reported in August.
