The best cold weather running gear
Using advice from the experts, I rounded up a list of cold running gear. All items below are recommended by experts or are highly rated and meet the requirements they said to look for.
Feetures Merino 10 Max Cushion Ankle Socks

Feetures makes some of our favorite no-show socks and this version is made from merino wool, which is particularly good for the winter months. “Wool, or wool-blend socks, keep your feet warm even if they get a little damp,” says Silva. These unisex socks have a seamless toe construction to prevent irritation and cushioning on the bottom for comfort, according to the brand.
Baleaf Thermal Fleece-Lined Shirt

NBC Selected editorial director, Lauren Swanson, has run multiple marathons and loves this thermal layer for winter training and beyond. “When I wear this shirt, I am rarely cold,” says Swanson. “Running in it feels cozy, but I’ll also wear it on particularly cold NYC mornings.” It’s made of polyester and spandex, so the fabric has a nice stretch to it, too, which is great for layering.
Hoka Mafate 5 Sneakers

These sneakers made our list of the best trail shoes thanks to their water-resistant and comfortable cushioned soles and deep lugs. Even if you aren’t technically hitting the trails, they can be a good option for cold-weather running. “If you’re running in snow or slushy conditions, trail shoes with extra grip or shoes with a water-resistant upper make a huge difference,” says Silva. These shoes are available in men’s and women’s sizes.
Brooks Momentum Thermal Tight 2.0

NBC Selected reporter Zoe Malin, who runs regularly, says that these tights never get itchy or slip. They have pockets for convenient storage and a wide waistband with an internal drawstring for a customized fit that keeps them in place as you move, according to the brand. They’re also sweat-resistant and are thin enough to be layered under sweats or other pants for added warmth on really frigid days.
On Weather Jacket

This running jacket is available in versions for men and women and is from NBC Selected editor-favorite brand On. The lightweight jacket is made from wind- and water-resistant material and has hidden airflow vents to prevent sweating. Because it is so lightweight, it is a good jacket to wear over other layers. It also folds up small into its own pocket, so you can easily pack it for runs while you’re traveling.

This adjustable belt has pockets for your phone, keys, credit cards and two 10-ounce water bottles, which will help remind you to stay hydrated on colder runs. The belt is lined with silica gel to minimize chafing and bouncing while you jog, and the outer portion has reflectors to keep you visible in the early morning or during the evening.

These gloves are lightweight and made from a fabric blend that is specifically meant to help you regulate your temperature, according to the brand. The fabric also has stretch to provide a snug fit and is touchscreen compatible, so you don’t need to take them off if you want to change the song on your phone or answer a text.
Melasa Beanie Hat with Light

Solve two common cold weather running problems with this hat. How to dress for running in cold weather

Dressing to run in low temperatures goes beyond just picking the right pieces like the ones above — how you utilize them matters, too. Our experts shared exactly how to get dressed to stay warm when you head outside for a run during the colder months.

“When you first step outside, you should feel a bit cold,” says Silva. “If you feel cozy right away, you’ve probably overdressed and will be uncomfortable once your body heats up.” Layering is the smartest thing you can do to prevent this — not only can it keep you cozy, but it allows you to peel layers off to prevent yourself from overheating if you start to get warm as you run. Here, the layers you should consider:

Base layer: A moisture-wicking base layer — like a shirt or leggings made of merino wool or synthetic fabrics — will help keep sweat off your skin, preventing chill when you slow down or stop, says Silva. This layer should be relatively thin so you can layer on top of it without feeling bulky.Mid-layer: If it’s below freezing, adding a thermal shirt or fleece pullover on top of your base layer will add extra warmth.Outer layer: A wind- and water-resistant jacket like On’s Weather Jacket will help keep out the cold and keep the warmth you create close to your body. Select one that you can zip up or down as you move to stay warmer or cool down a bit, says Silva.

If you like to listen to music or carry your phone while running, consider touchscreen-friendly gloves, like the New Balance Performance Touchscreen Gloves.

title: Trump administration spent $9.5B last year on employee leave, driven by DOGE-era cuts
summary: The Trump administration spent $9.5 billion last year on paid administrative leave as it pushed to cut costs, the Government Accountability Office said.
story: The Trump administration spent an estimated $9.5 billion last year on paid administrative leave for federal workers as it pushed to cut costs by shrinking the government, according to a Government Accountability Office report released Tuesday.

Agencies’ use of paid administrative leave jumped by 435% from 2023 to 2025, the report found, and salary costs from such leave rose sixfold. That coincides with President Donald Trump’s decision in 2025 to create the Department of Government Efficiency led by tech billionaire Elon Musk, which enacted mass firings and dissolved the U.S. Agency for International Development.

Much of the increased leave cost — about $6.7 billion — came from  salary paid through a DOGE-era “deferred resignation program,” GAO found. Nearly 140,000 federal employees opted into the program, according to the Office of Personnel Management. It allowed for federal workers who agreed to quit in early 2025 to still be paid through September.
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the report.

The GAO report emphasized that its numbers were estimates, noting that OPM “does not know the actual costs of the paid administrative leave used for workforce reduction efforts, including the deferred resignation program.”

“To calculate long-term savings, OPM needs to know short-term costs of paid administrative leave used for these efforts,” the report explained. “However, OPM cannot easily and accurately do this because the paid administrative leave used for workforce reduction efforts is reported with other types of general paid administrative leave.”

The deferred resignation program was unveiled just days into Trump’s second term, and federal workers received a “Fork in the Road” email laying out their options. Musk, who had quickly risen to the highest echelons of power in the administration, had previously sent an email with the same subject line to X employees, where he reshaped the company’s workforce.

At the time of the program’s announcement, then-White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said that if federal workers “don’t want to work in the office and contribute to making America great again, then they are free to choose a different line of work, and the Trump Administration will provide a very generous payout of 8 months.”

During Trump’s second term, the federal workforce has lost more than 271,000 employees as of July, according to data published by OPM. The figure includes voluntary and involuntary departures. The data indicates that between 2015, the earliest year provided, and 2025, when Trump took office again, the federal workforce grew every year.

title: Trump’s handpicked Kennedy Center board votes to immediately close venue for renovations
summary: The vote came the same day that Chief Financial Officer Donna Kauranen resigned from her position, two sources familiar with the matter told NBC News.
story: President Donald Trump’s handpicked Kennedy Center board voted Tuesday to immediately shutter the performing arts center, citing its “dire” financial and structural shape.

The vote came shortly after a federal judge in Washington rejected the board’s latest effort to add Trump’s name to the building’s facade. The Trump administration appealed the judge’s ruling Tuesday night.
Trump said on social media after the vote that renovations wouldn’t happen unless his name was added to the building.

“The closing will take place immediately, however, the Renovation and Reconstruction, which is a very large and complex job, cannot begin until such time as the D.C. Circuit rules on the Board’s approved name,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. “If the ruling is a negative one, which it should not be, and is not overturned by the U.S. Supreme Court, the Reconstruction and the Renovation of The Kennedy Center will not take place.”

“In the meantime, 17 Million Dollars, raised by President Trump, has been put into The Kennedy Center account to keep it afloat,” he added. Congress appropriated $250 million for the project last year.
The board had cited a partial ceiling collapse in the center’s Grand Foyer this month as evidence that the center needed to be immediately closed for repairs.

A construction consultant and the center’s director “consider the main building to be unsafe for continued occupancy, and anticipate further risk to the public and employees if the building is not immediately closed and renovations begun,” the board said in a draft resolution to close the center for two years.

It was the third time since February that the board has voted to close the center for renovations for two years. Rep. Joyce Beatty, D-Ohio, an ex officio board member, has challenged those efforts in court, saying the board hadn’t done its due diligence before it decided it needed to close the venue.
The center was initially scheduled to close July 5.

Attorneys for the board have said the legal action has kept them from doing necessary repairs, but the judge presiding over the case noted at a hearing Tuesday — as he had previously — that his earlier order preventing full closure allowed for emergency repairs.

Trump, who was elected chairman last year by the board he appointed, joined the closed-door meeting virtually and spent several minutes criticizing both Beatty and the judge who blocked his name from being added to the facade, according to a source who dialed into the Zoom meeting and who opposes the closure.

That person described Trump as getting into a shouting match with Beatty, whom he blasted as an “obstructionist” who didn’t know how to get things done. Beatty countered that Trump was unprofessional, and at one point each accused the other of incompetence, the source said.

During the tirade, Trump also suggested without evidence that the judge, Christopher Cooper, is compromised because his wife, an attorney, represented former President Joe Biden, the source said. Trump also suggested there was something untoward about the judge’s wife’s not using her husband’s last name, the source said.

Attorneys for the center are expected to ask the judge to lift his block on closing the center this week. A source familiar with Beatty’s legal strategy said her attorneys will oppose the move and argue that the repairs can be done without shutting down the center.

In a separate resolution that was originally scheduled to be taken up Tuesday, as well, the Kennedy Center said that it “is in a dire financial position” and facing potential bankruptcy after it “exhausted its fiscal resources” — and that only Trump can rescue it.
The board had said that to do so, he would have to be recognized for his efforts on the exterior of the building.

“The Kennedy Center is in such a precarious fiscal position that it will not be able to support its payroll obligations, nor routine maintenance contracts within a matter of weeks,” said the draft resolution, which was made public in a court filing. “While actively considering alternative means of fiscal survival, President Trump has offered to step in and raise the necessary funds to keep the Center from bankruptcy during its much needed renovation.”

“With certain fiscal collapse within weeks, the board seeks to determine what recognition and acknowledgement will comply” with the judge’s earlier order banning the center from being renamed the Donald J. Trump and John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts.
The board didn’t vote on the resolution at the meeting because members said they needed to focus on the closure issue.

The Kennedy Center’s chief financial officer, Donna Kauranen, resigned from her position Tuesday, two sources familiar with the matter told NBC News. She had served in the role for about 18 months and was brought on in early 2025 by the center’s former executive director, Richard Grenell, after serving in budget and finance roles for several Republican governors around the country over the past two decades.
A spokesperson for the Kennedy Center did not immediately respond to a request for comment Tuesday night on Kauranen’s resignation.

The trustees had voted last month to instead add the words “renovated and restored by President Donald J. Trump” to the building and to rename the center’s grounds President Donald J. Trump Plaza by Sept. 8. The new draft resolution offered numerous similar suggestions.
In a ruling issued just ahead of the board vote, Cooper, the judge, found the effort to add Trump’s name to the facade in a different way was also illegal.

“Simply put, Defendants cannot install memorials for President Trump or anyone or anything else at the Kennedy Center without Congress’s blessing. The board resolution bucks a federal court order and a statute Congress enacted,” Cooper said.
He also noted the board’s threat about fundraising — and its claim that the center might need to be razed if Trump’s repair plan isn’t followed — with skepticism.

The “government offered ‘no proof that current or future donations hinge on President Trump’s name being on the building’ and ‘no competent evidence that removing the Trump name would prevent the Center from fulfilling its artistic mission, as it has done for the last sixty years,’” he wrote.
Instead, Cooper suggested, the opposite could be true.

“The renaming of the Center coincided with declines in revenue and contributions, as artists cancelled performances, the Washington National Opera ended its 50-year residency, and ticket sales and viewership of the Kennedy Center Honors broadcast dropped precipitously. The Board also has access to the $257 million that Congress appropriated for necessary capital improvements,” he wrote, but that’s “beside the point for present purposes.”
And while cultural institutions often honor big donors by naming buildings or features after them, Cooper said, “Congress had other ideas for the Kennedy Center.”

“It limited such memorials and donor recognitions to discrete (and discreet) areas, so as not to detract from the Center’s function as an ongoing memorial to President Kennedy. The current Board’s apparent disagreement with that approach does not change the law,” he wrote.

Cooper said he could “not license a violation of those authorities under threat that some unidentified donors will withhold their largesse if the Board is not allowed to have its way. It can even less reward a decision by Board members, including the Chair, to curb the Center’s fundraising efforts because they cannot abide statutory restrictions on displaying his name.”

Beatty praised Cooper’s ruling in a statement, saying: “The law is extremely clear: The John F. Kennedy Center is named for President Kennedy — and no one else. But President Trump is holding the Kennedy Center hostage unless he can put his name on this sacred memorial.”
“This unlawfulness is as breathtaking as it is wrong, and it needs to stop,” she said.
Her attorneys, Norm Eisen of Democracy Defenders Action and Nathaniel Zelinsky of Washington Litigation Group, said in a joint statement, “Legal sanity has once again prevailed over Trump’s vanity.”

Roma Daravi, vice president for public relations at the Kennedy Center, said in a statement that in addition to appealing, they intend to “move forward with recognizing Chairman President Trump’s historic contributions to the revitalization of America’s Cultural Center.”

title: Judge Judy’s Tough-Love Message of Empowerment, Delivered on TODAY in 1996
summary: Judge Judy spoke with TODAY in 1999 about her then-new book about empowering women and what it is about “Judge Judy” that people liked so much.
story: Welcome to the “TODAY Archives,” where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment highlights Judge Judy Sheindlin, who stopped by the show on Feb. 1, 1999 to promote a new book designed to lift up women.
Court shows were nothing new when “Judge Judy” premiered on Sept. 16, 1996, but she took it a new level.

Her harsh treatment toward those in her courtroom and her abrasive comments made Judge Judy — real name Judith Sheindlin — a favorite of daytime TV. By the time she visited TODAY on Feb. 1, 1999, the show was a hit and she was a bona fide star.
“You’re, what, the number one rated syndicated show?” Katie Couric asked.
“So they tell me these days,” Sheindlin replied.

Sheindlin remained on the show for nearly 25 years before the final episode aired in July 2021. She moved on to headline the Amazon Prime spinoff, “Judy Justice,” which will come to an end after Sheindlin announced her retirement earlier this week.
When Sheindlin stopped by TODAY, she wasn’t just talking about the law or her program, though. She was promoting her book, “Beauty Fades, Dumb Is Forever,” which was aimed at helping women.
Why Did She Write ‘Beauty Fades, Dumb Is Forever’?
Sheindlin was befuddled by some of the women she’d encountered in her courtroom during her career and felt she had to impart some of her wisdom.

“Fifty percent of the people in this country are women, and it struck me over the course of my career that they weren’t having half the fun, they weren’t getting half the compensation, they weren’t getting half the appreciation, and there were a lot of dumb things that I saw parading through my courtroom over the last 25 or 28 years,” she said.

“So I decided to memorialize some of my thoughts and some of my personal experiences because I didn’t do things right all the time myself, in a book that hopefully people will read, laugh a little bit, and take something away with.”
What Did Sheindlin Say About Women Being Victims?

Sheindlin marveled at how women “subjugate themselves in the workplace,” even if they’re smarter than men and that they often want to be liked to the point it’s counterproductive. She also urged women to take more responsibility for their own actions.

“Stop being a victim. There aren’t victims. If you do something stupid, it’s your fault. Move on with it,” she said. “If you allow a guy to move into your house, and he is sucking up all your money, and sucking up all of your energy, and not giving you anything back — if you allow that situation to continue, it’s your fault. Don’t make yourself a victim.”
Why Did Judge Judy Think People Liked Her Show?
Sheindlin, of course, did spend some time chatting up her program and just why it appealed to viewers.
“I think people like to see the right thing happen at the end of a trial, and they’ve seen over the last decade, trials that took interminably long and left a very unsatisfying result,” she said.
“A trial to me was always supposed to be the search for the truth. It wasn’t supposed to be a game, and I like to get there and get there fast.”

title: Kit Harington Explains Why He Wanted to Be Part of HBO ‘Harry Potter’ Show Amid Backlash
summary: Kit Harington opened up about joining the upcoming second season of HBO’s “Harry Potter” series amid controversy over author J.K.
story: Kit Harington opened up about joining the upcoming second season of HBO’s “Harry Potter” series amid controversy over author J.K. Rowling and the decision to reboot a beloved film series for television.

The “Industry” star will play Gilderoy Lockhart, a wizard and teacher at Hogwarts, in Season 2, based on the book “Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets.” Kenneth Branagh played Lockhart in the 2002 film of the same name.
TODAY’s Craig Melvin asked Harington, currently starring in MGM+’s “A Tale of Two Cities,” why he wanted to be a part of the “Harry Potter” series, despite pushback against it.

“I’ve been a lifelong Harry Potter fan,” Harington said. “I was a fan when I was a kid, and then I rediscovered it as an adult, listening to it every night. I listen to it every single night, and it helps me go to sleep, and I know other people do that as well, so they’re really important books to me.”
Harington notably voices Lockhart in a full-cast audio edition of “Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets,” released by Audible in December 2025.

Nicholas Hoult was originally cast as Lockhart for Season 2, HBO announced Aug. 11. Two weeks later, the official Instagram account for the show announced Harington will step into the role due to scheduling conflicts.

The first season of the new HBO show, based on “Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone,” will premiere on Christmas Day. HBO shared a sneak peek photo on March 24 of actor Dominic McLaughlin in costume as Harry Potter, wearing a red Gryffindor robe. The first trailer was released the same day.

“When I knew this was happening as a series, I thought it was the best idea,” Harington said on TODAY. “I love the films, but with this, they can really explore the books at their fullest, and for a book nerd like me, that was a really great idea.
“So it was one that I had eyes on, I really wanted to be in it, and the part I’m playing is just the best,” he added.
Actors Rafe Spall (Arthur Weasley), Jasper Ambrose (Colin Creevey) and Molly Hewitt-Richards (Moaning Myrtle) have also joined the cast of Season 2, according to Variety.

The ambitious HBO series looks to adapt all seven of the “Harry Potter” books for the screen, but it has faced controversy since it was announced. Some fans say another adaptation is unnecessary after the books were adapted into eight films, released from 2001-2011.

Other backlash stems from the show’s ties to “Harry Potter” author J.K. Rowling, who’s made comments characterized by critics as anti-transgender. Directors Kate Herron and Ally Pankiw both wrote on social media that they had been approached to work on the “Harry Potter” series and turned it down due to Rowling’s views, according to The Hollywood Reporter.
Rowling will serve as an executive producer of the new series.

title: Emilio Estevez and Charlie Sheen Reunite With ‘Young Guns’ Cast 38 Years After Film’s Release
summary: Charlie Sheen and Emilio Estevez reunited with “Young Guns” castmates Kiefer Sutherland, Lou Diamond Phillips, Dermot Mulroney and others at a fan convention.
story: They may not be quite as young as they used to be, but the cast of “Young Guns” still got it.
Emilio Estevez and brother Charlie Sheen reunited with the cast of the 1988 movie last week at Fan Expo in Dallas.
Co-star Dermot Mulroney posted a photo of the group on his Instagram page Sept. 13.
“38 years later #youngguns rides again — PALS,” he captioned the picture, which featured him, along with Estevez, Sheen, Kiefer Sutherland, Lou Diamond Phillips, Terry O’Quinn and Casey Siemaszko.
Mulroney posted another carousel of photos with his co-stars from the event.

“PALS since 1877 — turns out we all have different sides of the same memories!,” he wrote. “Laughed our asses off this weekend. When @kiefersutherland says ‘never had more fun on a movie’ you know @you had some fun!”

“Young Guns” starred Estevez as the Billy the Kid in a fictionalized story about him and the Regulators, a group of young men working for a rancher. It marked the first of several movies Estevez and Sheen made together. The film was a hit and spawned a 1990 sequel, “Young Guns II.”
Estevez also posted a picture of the reunion on Instagram, captioning it, “REGULATORS...Mount up.”

In 2025, Estevez, who reunited with the cast of “The Breakfast Club” that same year, spoke about his plans to make a third “Young Guns” film. While several characters had previously died, he said Phillips would return, as would Christian Slater who appeared in the sequel.

“It does center on a bunch of new regulators,” he told Josh Horowitz on the “Happy Sad Confused” podcast. “Mostly Latino. Indigenous people. Most of the film takes place in Mexico. And it falls on the eve of the Mexican Revolution.”
Estevez has been known for not taking part in cast reunions, a decision he said is considered a bigger deal than it actually is.
“To use the word ‘avoid’ is not, I don’t think, the correct word to use. It just hasn’t been top of mind,” he told Horowitz.

title: How to Watch Night 2 of the ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Season 35 Premiere

story: “Dancing with the Stars” is back!

Viewers got to return to the ballroom Sept. 15 for the first episode of Season 35’s two-night special premiere, which saw the male competitors take the floor. One person has already been eliminated, despite a voting glitch.
Then, the action continues on Wednesday, Sept. 16 with part two, set to introduce viewers to the female contestants and their partners.

Sixteen new celebrities, including Jenna Dewan, Ciara Miller, Julia Stiles, Tatyana Ali and Taylor Hanson, are joining their professional dance partners to compete for the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy.
Judges Carrie Ann Inaba, Bruno Tonioli and Derek Hough returned to critique the teams alongside co-hosts Alfonso Ribeiro and Julianne Hough.

summary: For the two-night season premiere of “Dancing With the Stars,” the men stepped onto the ballroom to kick off Season 35.
story: “Dancing With the Stars” Season 35 has officially kicked off!
This year’s show began with an unexpected twist: the male celebrities would only be competing during the Sept. 15 premiere.
The two-night Season 35 kickoff divided the 16 competing couples into two groups, with each night ending in an elimination.
The episode opened with a special performance choreographed by co-host Julianne Hough, who then reunited with Alfonso Ribeiro to welcome viewers to the new “DWTS” season.
The couples then danced to a song from the year they were born, with judges Carrie Ann Inaba, Bruno Tonioli and Derek Hough giving them a 1-10 score.
In an unplanned moment, Hough updated fans during the broadcast that online voting was experiencing technical difficulties, and that only votes via text would be accepted.
Here’s a recap of what went down on night one of the Season 35 “DWTS” premiere, including the dances and scores of each couple.
What Did Each Star Dance to and What Was Their Score?

Tyler Cameron with partner Sharna Burgess will perform a tango to “Are You Gonna Go My Way” by Lenny Kravitz — SCORE: 17/30Ezra Frech with partner Daniella Karagach will perform a tango to “Since U Been Gone” by Kelly Clarkson — SCORE: 20/30Taylor Hanson with partner Britt Stewart will perform a quickstep to “Tell Her About It” by Billy Joel — SCORE: 16/30Conner Leavitt with partner Adele Zaikman will perform a salsa to “Whoomp! There It Is” by Tag Team — SCORE: 12/30Jackson Olson with partner Emma Slater will perform a cha cha to “Wannabe” by Spice Girls — SCORE: 15/30Guillermo Rodriguez with partner Witney Carson will perform a cha cha to “Mr. Big Stuff” by Jean Knight — SCORE: 10/30Harry Shum Jr. with partner Jenna Johnson will perform a cha cha to “Let’s Groove” by Earth, Wind & Fire — SCORE: 21/30Connor Wood with partner Rylee Arnold will perform a cha cha to “I Like It, I Love It” by Tim McGraw — SCORE: 16/30
Tyler Cameron with partner Sharna Burgess will perform a tango to “Are You Gonna Go My Way” by Lenny Kravitz — SCORE: 17/30
Ezra Frech with partner Daniella Karagach will perform a tango to “Since U Been Gone” by Kelly Clarkson — SCORE: 20/30
Taylor Hanson with partner Britt Stewart will perform a quickstep to “Tell Her About It” by Billy Joel — SCORE: 16/30
Conner Leavitt with partner Adele Zaikman will perform a salsa to “Whoomp! There It Is” by Tag Team — SCORE: 12/30
Jackson Olson with partner Emma Slater will perform a cha cha to “Wannabe” by Spice Girls — SCORE: 15/30
Guillermo Rodriguez with partner Witney Carson will perform a cha cha to “Mr. Big Stuff” by Jean Knight — SCORE: 10/30
Harry Shum Jr. with partner Jenna Johnson will perform a cha cha to “Let’s Groove” by Earth, Wind & Fire — SCORE: 21/30
Connor Wood with partner Rylee Arnold will perform a cha cha to “I Like It, I Love It” by Tim McGraw — SCORE: 16/30
Who Is At the Top of the Leaderboard?
After the first night, Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson landed at the top of the leaderboard. The two received 7s from each judge for a total of 21 out of 30.
The two celebrated their achievement, especially Shum who shared in his rehearsal video that he was worried about being a great partner.
Was There An Elimination?
Yes, at the end of the episode one couple was eliminated.
After only getting the chance to perform once, Conner Leavitt partner Adele Zaikman took their last bow.
“This has been the most fun. I have the greatest dance partner in the world in Adele. I can’t wait for the world to see her talent,” Leavitt said after they were eliminated.
On Wednesday, Sept. 16, the ladies will get a chance to show off their moves. The judges’ scores will be combined with the live viewer votes to determine which couple will also be eliminated.
How to Vote for the ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Contestants
Usually, fans will be able to vote for their favorite couple during the live simulcast of the show in the ET/CT time zones by heading to the “Dancing With the Stars” website.
However, during the Sept. 15 broadcast co-host Julianne Hough informed viewers online voting was down and that audiences needed to vote via text. Votes through the website did not count.
Throughout the season, U.S. viewers can vote by SMS/text message during the live voting window each episode/week. Voting by text cannot be changed and only the first 10 count.
If voting online, viewers get up to 10 votes and can change and save their votes throughout the telecast.
Voting is only open at this time for the male celebrities who performed on Sept. 15. Tomorrow, during the live telecast, viewers can vote for the female celebrities competing.

title: Does Taylor Swift’s ‘SVU’ Skit Have a Secret Message to Her Fans?
summary: What could “saccharide, Aries, from the vineyard, north or south” really mean? Taylor Swift’s “SVU” skit at the Emmys has her fans speculating about Easter Eggs.
story: “Saccharide. Aries. From the vineyard. North or south.”

These arbitrary phrases have left Swifties everywhere with dozens of questions after the Emmy Awards, the main one being: Is Taylor Swift the mastermind her fans know her to be, or did she just send them on a wild goose chase?

Clues point to the former. But first, let’s rewind for those who need it: Mariska Hargitay had hosted the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards on Sept. 14 and had tapped Swift, her friend and longtime “Law & Order: SVU” fan, to appear in an “SVU” parody skit that aired during the telecast.
The pre-taped sketch features Hargitay, Ice-T, Kelli Giddish, Peter Scanavino and more actors playing their characters from the crime drama. Their case to crack: Will Taylor Swift attend the Emmys?

Hargitay, as Olivia Benson, brought up as evidence Swift’s love of Easter eggs. She wheeled out a crime board filled with clues as each person took turns suggesting why certain nominees and shows pointed toward Swift making a surprise appearance.
Suddenly, a crime board was wheeled away to reveal Swift was standing in the precinct.
“Hey guys, this isn’t adding up,” she said while wearing a gray suit and holding a coffee mug.
Ice-T rebuffed her input. “And who asked you, rookie?” he said.
She replied, “Our perp has a clear M.O. A lot of this doesn’t fit the pattern, and I don’t think everything is a clue.”
“It is to the Swifties,” Hargitay quickly replied.
“I think what we’re going to be looking for is hiding in plain sight,” Swift replied.
She then panned and spoke directly to the camera: “Saccharide. Aries. From the vineyard. North or south.”
“What did you just say?” Hargitay asked her.
“I didn’t say anything,” Swift said with a shrug.

While the sketch wraps by cracking its case — Swift won’t be at the Emmys because she’ll be busy supporting husband Travis Kelce at the Chiefs season opener — the meaning of Swift’s spoken message is still a mystery.
Swifties of course know that nothing is ever that simple when it comes to the singer. They immediately began dissecting the skit on social media, seeing if they could decode a secret message.
What could it mean? Well, the Emmys executive producers have confirmed that the words have some type of significance because they were specifically chosen by Swift.

After the Emmys, executive producers Jesse Collins, Dionne Harmon and Jeannae Rouzon-Clay from Jesse Collins Entertainment, and NBCUniversal live events and specials exec VP Jen Neal, spoke with reporters and explained how they pulled off the sketch.
“Taylor loved the script and she had some thoughts and we worked that in,” Collins told reporters, according to Variety.
One of Swift’s notes was to add Easter eggs, Collins revealed.
“She wanted them to be really official. And correct,” Rouzan-Clay shared.

As always, Swifties are on the case, and they might’ve already cracked it. Many shared their theories on social media that the sketch pointed to Swift releasing the long-awaited “Taylor’s Versions” from her debut and “Reputation” albums.
One Swiftie said on X that Ice-T’s “rookie” line and Aries, the first astrological sign, reference her self-titled first album.

Another zoomed in on the crime board and noticed a Post-it note that read “Is it TV?” adding more fuel to the fire. The board also had a heart similar to the one Swift used to draw on the back of her hand during the early days of her career.
Beneath the post, one X user replied, “Olivia said ‘the answer has been TV this whole time’ also.”
But others were more convinced that “Reputation (Taylor’s Version)” is on the way.

“I believe Debut TV is next but to add fuel to the Rep TV fire (no pun intended), if you go all the way back to the Karma MV in the Reputation scene Taylor wears the ram mask and the ram is the Aries zodiac animal,” one tweeted.
Over on Reddit, the speculation continued.
“I’m putting in my guess now — these are Rep vault track titles,” one suggested.
And one fan had a wild but plausible idea.
“OMG GUYS THERES TWO BOARDS!!! TWO!!” they said. “We are getting both Debut and Rep.”
Looks like we’ll have to wait for Swift’s next message to see what other tricks she has up her sleeve.

title: All About Keri Russell and Matthew Rhys’ Relationship, From How They Met to ‘The Americans’
summary: On screen, Keri Russell and Matthew Rhys paired a pair of married Russian spies living undercover in “The Americans,” which ran from 2013 to 2018 on FX.
story: On screen, Keri Russell and Matthew Rhys paired a pair of married Russian spies living undercover in “The Americans,” which ran from 2013 to 2018 on FX.
Off screen, the “Felicity” star and the Welsh actor were falling in love.

While “The Americans” was still airing in 2017, the couple spoke to People about making their relationship work. Russell said a bit of “alone time,” since they spend so much time together. Plus, Rhys said, “she has the patience of a saint, so that helps.”
Rhys and Russell turned heads at the 2026 Emmys, where they appeared on the red carpet together because they were both nominated for acting awards.

Russell was nominated for outstanding lead actress in a drama series for her role as Kate Wyler in “The Diplomat,” which she lost, and Rhys was nominated — and won — for both outstanding lead actor in a comedy series as Tom Loftis in “Widow’s Bay” and outstanding lead actor in a limited or anthology series or movie as Nile Jarvis in “The Beast in Me.”

But when the trophies where handed out, Rhys still felt that Russell came out on top. In a video captured by the Associated Press, he praised his longtime partner for her more measured approach to awards season: After joking that he tends to brag about his wins more than Russell, who is always supportive of her competitors, Rhys quipped, “She’s always really the winner, if I’m perfectly honest.”
Here’s what to know about their roughly 13-year-long relationship.
They Met Long Before “The Americans”
During a joint appearance on “Watch What Happens Live“ in 2017, Rhys and Russell recalled the first time they met.
Rhys said it was a “a very long, long time ago” — back when he was 26 years old.
“I very drunkenly asked her for her number when she was a young single slip of a thing,” Rhys said.
They had met after a “kickball party,” Russell said. The conversation happened in a parking lot after Russell asked Rhys to open up a beer for her.
Rhys gave more of the story in a 2023 appearance on “Watch What Happens Live.” He left her a drunken voice mail — to which she didn’t respond.
Their Romance Rekindled on ‘The Americans’
But “it took a while,” Rhys said of their love story on “Watch What Happens Live.”
Russell said that one day, after a “heavy dose of fight training,” Rhys told her, “We’ve met before.”
She responded, “No, we haven’t.” Rhys then reminded her about the “drunken message” he left her. “As soon as he said that, I knew exactly what he meant,” she said.
Russell said in a later interview with Variety in 2024 that they fell in love shooting the first season.
“I was in love with Matthew,” Russell said. “We were, like, hot and heavy in love, shooting the spy stuff at night in disguises and wigs. I mean, it was such a fun, sexy time. So fun, oh my gosh.”
They Kept Their Romance a Secret On Set
Rhys told Andy Cohen in a 2023 appearance on “Watch What Happens Live” that he and Russell kept their relationship private on set for “about a year.”
Rhys told People how they broke the news to their producers — not only that they were dating, but that they were expecting a baby. Their son, Sam, was born between Seasons 4 and 5.

“So when we told our producers like, ‘Oh, we do have something to say,’ they’re like, ‘Oh, don’t tell us you’re together.’ We’re like, ‘Actually, we’re going to have a baby.’ They were like, ‘Oh my God,’ because we’d kept it a secret for so long.”
Their Son, Sam, Was Born in 2016
Rhys and Russell welcomed their son, Sam, into the world in 2016. That year, Russell raved about their kid in an interview with TODAY. She said, “He’s so good. He’s big and fat and nice.”
Russell is also mom to two kids, River and Willa, from her marriage to her ex-husband, carpenter Shane Deary.
They’re Not Married — But Matthew Rhys Joked About Proposing in an Acceptance Speech

At the 2018 Emmys, Rhys won the award for outstanding lead actor in a drama series for his role in “The Americans.” When he was announced as the winner, the actor gave Russell a big kiss on before making his way to the stage.
Near the end of his acceptance speech, he peered out into the audience and thanked Russell.

“And finally, to the woman who truly got me this award, who just stands in front of me every day and just puts up with me. She said, ‘If you propose to me, I would punch you clean in the mouth.’ I don’t have the words or the time, neither which would do you justice, Keri Lynn, except thank you, more to come, thank you.”
They Were Both Nominated Multiple Times for ‘The Americans’
Keri Russell was up for an Emmy in 2016, 2017 and 2018 for “The Americans.” Rhys was nominated the same years but won in 2018.
When they were both up for Golden Globes for “The Americans” in 2019, the couple joked about their coordinated awards in an interview with with Ryan Seacrest for E! News.
“Thank God we don’t have to break up,” Russell joked.
They Recently Reunited on Screen for ‘Cocaine Bear’
In 2018, “The Americans” aired its final episode. They reunited on screen for the 2023 flick “Cocaine Bear.”

“I unashamedly jumped on my partner’s coattails because I knew (Keri Russell) was doing this movie with (director) Elizabeth Banks, who we know, and I read the script and I simply said, ‘Who’s playing that? That little fun part, a few seconds in the beginning?’ She goes, ‘I don’t know.’ I said, ‘Ask Banks.’ And then she said, ‘No, it’s been cast,’ and I said ‘Tell Banks I’ll do it.’ And then I was like, ‘Well actually, just ask her if I can do it,’” Rhys told The A.V. Club.
Rhys Supports Russell in Her ‘Diplomat’ Era
Rhys and Russell walked the red carpet together at the 2024 Golden Globes. That year, Russell was nominated for an Emmy for the Netflix drama “The Diplomat.” She’s up for an award again this year.
In an interview with Variety about her work in “The Diplomat,” Rhys gave an assessment of his partner’s personality.

“She is naturally a very shy person, and to expose herself in that way day after day, I think she finds both taxing and challenging. But she is a mind, and she loves being challenged, and she loves words — books are her biggest passion. Words and narrative are her great love.”

title: It’s the Great Pumpkin (Spice Latte), Charlie Brown: Starbucks Launches Peanuts Collection
summary: This pumpkin spice season, Starbucks is rolling out the limited-edition Peanuts + Starbucks collection items featuring a Snoopy glass cold cup.
story: The Peanuts gang is celebrating the arrival of the Great Pumpkin ... Spice Latte.

Starbucks is marking the return of everything pumpkin spice this fall by rolling out 10 collectible items featuring Snoopy, Charlie Brown and company as part of its limited-edition Peanuts + Starbucks collection.

Starbucks locations around the world will be selling the collectibles while supplies last. The collection coincides with the 60th anniversary of the classic, Halloween-themed Peanuts show “It’s the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown.”

The headliner is a Snoopy glass cold cup with the iconic “Peanuts” character wearing a winter hat and orange beanie with his pal Woodstock perched on the top of the straw. The Snoopy glass follows the viral Starbucks Bearista cup, which caused a frenzy in 2025, was dressed up for the World Cup in July and turned pink in a separate promotion.
Here’s what to know about the Peanuts + Starbucks collection, as well as the two limited-edition, Peanuts-themed beverages that Starbucks is selling.

title: All 13 of Mariska Hargitay’s Emmys Looks — Including 1 That Honors Mom Jayne Mansfield
summary: Take a look at all of the outfits Mariska Hargitay wore as she hosted the Emmy Awards.
story: When someone says Mariska Hargitay is the hostess with the mostest, they may be referring to the number of outfits she wore.

The “Law & Order: SVU” star hosted the Emmy Awards for the first time on Sept. 14 and proceeded to wear at least 13 different outfits during the evening — and that doesn’t include what she sported in her pre-taped sketch with Taylor Swift.

Hargitay first walked the red carpet in a flowing red sequined gown with one strap hanging off her shoulder. It matched a red sparkly dress worn by her daughter, Amaya, 15, for the occasion. The Emmys carpet was a true family affair for Hargitay, who was also joined by husband Peter Hermann and their sons August, 20, and Andrew, 14.

Many fans pointed out that Hargitay and Amaya’s red dresses seemingly re-created a red dress the Emmy host’s mother, Jayne Mansfield, wore in the 1956 musical, “The Girl Can’t Help It.” Before her hosting gig, Hargitay won two Emmys for her HBO documentary “My Mom Jayne.”
But Hargitay latest homage to her mom’s fashion was merely the beginning of her cavalcade of costumes, as she slipped into a shimmering, strapless off-white dress to deliver her opening monologue.

To open the show, she joked about the audience being full of former “SVU” guest stars, celebrated her status as the first female host in 15 years, and re-created Nicole Kidman’s famous AMC ad to honor TV storytelling.
Throughout the night, Hargitay made frequent costume changes, including a sleek black gown with matching gloves, a satin white suit and a fur-lined cape paired with a sword.
Take a look at some of Hargitay’s fashion highlights worn over the course of the evening:
As the evening wound down, Hargitay said she enjoyed the experience.
“It’s been an absolute delight to be your host,” she said as the show drew to a close. “Thank you for all the love and joy tonight.
“And now that we’ve reached the end, there’s only one thing left to do,” she said as the iconic “dun, dun” from “Law & Order: SVU” played.
“God, I love it when it does that!”

title: Yes, Witney Carson Is Pregnant. And Yes, She Will Still Be Competing on ‘DWTS’: ‘It’s a Big Blessing to Do Both’
summary: On Aug. 17, “Dancing With the Stars” announced that pro dancer Witney Carson would be paired with Guillermo Rodriguez for Season 35.
story: On Aug. 17, “Dancing With the Stars” announced that pro dancer Witney Carson would be paired with Guillermo Rodriguez for Season 35. That same day, she revealed she was pregnant with her third child.

The announcement had many people wondering how she would be able to compete since the new season didn’t start for another month. But as Carson tells TODAY.com, she and husband Carson McAllister were set on expanding their family, and she didn’t think she needed to put her career on hold.

“We decided we wanted to grow our family. It’s time,” Carson, mom to sons Kevin, 5, and Jet, 3, says. “We know that we want a lot of kids and we thought it was a perfect year to start doing that. Then this opportunity came up again to do the show, and it just felt like, ‘You know what? I kind of want to prove to myself that I can do both!’ And I love both.”

Dancing since she was a child, Carson first gained fame after competing on Season 9 of “So You Think You Can Dance” in 2012.  The following year, she joined the “DWTS” troupe, before being promoted to a pro for Season 18 in 2014.

“I love to dance, and I love to compete, and I want to grow my family, as well,” the 32-year-old says. “I don’t feel like people necessarily have to lose parts of themselves to keep growing their family. That’s kind of my mantra. I’m gonna stay true to what I love and continue on my career and continue to grow my family. It’s a big blessing to be able to do both.”
For now, Carson is “feeling good,” listening to her body and making sure her baby’s healthy.

“As much as I want to dance and want to do all of it, I really have to be careful to make sure that I don’t overdo it,” she notes. “It’s perfectly safe to do all the things and I’m really not taking this any differently than I would any other season as far as mentally and physically.”

Taking it week by week, among her priorities is making sure she and her growing family are properly fueled. With a jam-packed schedule full of rehearsals and taking care of her boys with another on the way, Carson says she’s grateful for her Campbell’s partnership and the ability to make easy meals for her family.
“I remember my mom always making a hot meal with Campbell’s and so it’s very nostalgic for me,” she says. “It goes back to my childhood.”

Season 35 of “DWTS” kicks off on Sept. 15, which coincides with Campbell’s Two-Step Tuesdays launch celebrating its new sauces. Carson notes that after making a meal with the lemon garlic option, “Everyone gobbled it up ... I love to make dinner. I love doing that for my family. But I don’t have a lot of time, so being able to do something really simple like this two-step dinner is just an absolute dream.”
What is taking more than just two steps is preparing for her and Rodriguez’s competition debut. During the first episode, the duo will perform a cha cha to “Mr. Big Stuff” by Jean Knight.

“I’m really just having fun and Guillermo’s obviously very funny, he’s very heartwarming, he’s adorable,” she says of the “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” star. “He’s already so loved, and honestly, I’m really taking this season no differently than I would any other season. And I think people are a little surprised that you can continue to dance the way that I have.”

Last season, Carson took home her second Mirrorball trophy after coming in first place with Robert Irwin. While many might underestimate her and the comedian’s chances, she could go far depending on votes. (Let’s not forget how Andy Richter was dubbed “the People’s Princess” and made it to the quarterfinals.)

“There’s a TikTok floating around that’s ... not of me, but it’s of a pregnant woman and she’s got a big belly, and she’s break dancing on it,” Carson says. “And the meme is like, ‘Witney, when she makes it to the finale,’ and I’m like, ‘Oh my gosh, literally!’”
With the possibility of her baby being crowned the youngest “DWTS” champ, Carson is ready for this new adventure.
“Listen, I’m prepared for it, kind of,” she says with a laugh. “I’ve never danced this far pregnant ... But listen, I will make it happen. I mean, I’m not injured. I’m just pregnant.”

title: Emily St. John Mandel’s ‘Exit Party’ Envisions Hope in a U.S. Torn Apart by Civil War. Read the First Page
summary: Read the first page of Emily St. John Mandel’s new novel “Exit Party.” The author breaks down the book’s setting and themes.
story: It is a truth universally acknowledged that a good story starts with a good first line. In TODAY’s “Cold Open,” authors tease their buzzy upcoming release by revealing and explaining its first line, paragraph or page.
Emily St. John Mandel has always been interested in the aftermath of catastrophe.
The acclaimed author of “Station Eleven” doesn’t waste any time getting to that cataclysm on the opening page of her new novel, “Exit Party,” which hits stores on Sept. 15.
“In the first spring after the collapse of the United States, the blossoming of the jacaranda trees felt to Ari like grace."
Mandel tells TODAY.com she wanted the novel’s very first line to have a “shock effect.”

“I just wanted to avoid confusion and plunge the reader immediately into this world I was creating,” Mandel tells TODAY.com. “It’s a very fast opening. We have the U.S. coming undone in literally the first sentence.”

It’s a theme Mandel has long explored in her work. In her 2014 bestseller “Station Eleven,” a group of survivors try to preserve art and human connection after the world is devastated by a deadly pandemic.
In “Exit Party,” a pair of connected storylines depict an “A side” of America splintered by civil war and a “B side” of a U.S. completely under totalitarian rule.

“I first started writing in the spring of 2022, and it seemed clear to me that I was extrapolating from our current world on the A side, where division turns into conflict,” Mandel says. “But by the time I finished the book about a year ago, I felt like I was struggling to stay ahead of the news cycle on the B side, the authoritarian state. The idea of America where secret police pick people off the street and disappear them felt fictional in 2022.”

“Exit Party” imagines how humans will try to retain connection and resilience in extreme circumstances, whether by throwing parties, putting on plays or performing a concert in a time of war or repression. Mandel says she was inspired by a 2016 story during the civil war in Syria in which residents in the war-torn town of Daraya assembled a secret underground library.
“You just want the characters to find these moments of brightness and ways to feel like you’re doing more than just surviving,” Mandel says.

The novel involves the ongoing journey of Aria, a character from her 2009 novel “The Singer’s Gun,” who has been released after 18 years in prison to an America divided by warring factions in the year 2031. She wanders a fractured Los Angeles, where the fighting has subsided for now.

“I think it’s important to me to try to kind of lean into these times when even though everything is wrong, there are moments that are good,” Mandel says. “This feeling of desperate joy at the end of the world.”
A primary theme of the novel is impermanence. A catastrophe has happened, but the characters work to find their way through to the other side of it.

“This idea that nothing lasts forever, and something always comes next after terrible moments we live through,” Mandel says. “It’s a book about resilience. Can you be resilient in these objectively awful times, because nothing lasts forever. Can you find hope in a state of impermanence?”

For those who enjoyed the Emmy-nominated “Station Eleven” television series in 2021-2022 on HBO Max, “Exit Party” is also being made for television. The feature project was bought by Laika Studios and will be produced by Amy Hodge of Fruit Tree, a film and television production company co-founded by Oscar winner Emma Stone and her husband, Dave McCary.
This time, Mandel, who did not work on the TV adaptation of “Station Eleven,” is adapting “Exit Party” for the screen.

“It’s been a challenge and fun,” she says. “I’ve always enjoyed revision, and for me, adaptation almost feels like a continuation of that. You realize pretty early on that you have to be willing to blow up the book to make it work onscreen.”
Read the First Page of Emily St. John Mandel’s ‘Exit Party’

In the first spring after the collapse of the United States, the blossoming of the jacaranda trees felt to Ari like grace. The trees bloomed in the same week that international peacekeeping troops withdrew from Los Angeles, and the convergence of flowers with the absence of foreign soldiers brought a delirious kind of hope. Everyone in the spring of 2031 knew the city was one terrorist attack away from disaster, but that peril made the season more vivid, not less.

It was Ari’s first spring outside of prison in nearly two decades, and she spent hours at a time walking the streets. Prison is a wasteland of sensory deprivation, and now the city was overwhelming. She kept expecting that the details of the world would cease to be extraordinary, but that kept not happening. No one around her seemed to notice the jacarandas, because in Los Angeles there are flowers every month of the year, but she walked streets where the trees were lit up by purple-blue blossoms and thought, My god. This place. She was forty-eight years old but felt younger, because so much of the world was new.

The United States had come undone following a coup d’état. Several states had seceded within a week of the coup, either alone or in alliances with neighbors, and war had broken out within the month. Now the fighting had subsided, for the most part, and Ari had been released into an uneasy aftermath.

title: Emmy Winners Full List 2026: Matthew Rhys, Jean Smart Make History as ‘Widow’s Bay’ Sweeps Awards
summary: See a full list of Emmys 2026 winners as the awards are broadcast from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles on Monday, Sept. 14.
story: The 78th annual Emmy Awards are officially over. This year, the awards were broadcast from Peacock Theater in Los Angeles on Monday, Sept. 14, and hosted by Mariska Hargitay.

Television fans found out which stars came out victorious in tough categories like outstanding lead actress in a drama series and outstanding lead actor in a comedy series. This year, Zendaya, Jean Smart, Sterling K. Brown, Noah Wyle and more received nominations. There were also 28 actors who received their first-ever Emmy nods.
Follow live coverage of the 2026 Emmys

Two actors in particular made history at the Emmys with their respective wins this year. Jean Smart became the first woman to win an Emmy for every season of a show with her fifth trophy for “Hacks”; and Matthew Rhys became the first person to win two leading acting Emmys for two different series in the same year.
Going into the night, “The Pitt” led the pack with 25 nominations. “Hacks” picked up 24 nods and new series “Widow’s Bay” impressed with 19.

A week before the Sept. 14 ceremony, a number of winners were announced at the Creative Arts Emmys. Hargitay took home two Emmys for her documentary “My Mom Jayne,” while Rob Reiner received a posthumous win for his role on “The Bear.” Bad Bunny, Shailene Woodley, David Harbour and Linda Cardellini were also winners headed into the night.
Who ended the evening with the most wins? See the list of nominees below to see who won.
Outstanding supporting actress in a comedy series
WINNER: Kate O’Flynn — “Widow’s Bay”
Dale Dickey — “Widow’s Bay”
Hannah Einbinder — “Hacks”
Janelle James — “Abbott Elementary”
Michelle Pfeiffer — “Margo’s Got Money Troubles”
Megan Stalter — “Hacks”
Jessica Williams — “Shrinking”
Outstanding lead actress in a comedy series
WINNER: Jean Smart — “Hacks”
Quinta Brunson — “Abbott Elementary”
Ayo Edebiri — “The Bear”
Elle Fanning — “Margo’s Got Money Troubles”
Lisa Kudrow — “The Comeback”
Outstanding lead actor in an anthology series or movie
WINNER: Matthew Rhys — “The Beast in Me”
Riz Ahmed — “Bait”
Jason Bateman — “Black Rabbit”
Charlie Hunnam — “Monster: The Ed Gein Story”

title: Catherine O’Hara and Rob Reiner Receive Moving Tributes During 2026 Emmys ‘In Memoriam’
summary: Catherine O’Hara and Rob Reiner received tributes at the 2026 Emmy Awards’ “In Memoriam” segment led by performers who were close to each of them.
story: Catherine O’Hara and Rob Reiner received tributes at the 2026 Emmy Awards’ “In Memoriam” segment led by performers who were close to each of them.

O’Hara’s former co-stars — Macaulay Culkin of “Home Alone” and Annie Murphy and Dan Levy of “Schitt’s Creek — celebrated the late actor in an emotional moment that began the segment. To start, Culkin, who as a child actor played O’Hara’s character’s son in the movie franchise, described the special connection the two shared.
Follow live coverage of the 2026 Emmys

“She was encouraging. She was warm. She was funny, but the word that I think of is ‘mama.’ You know, she wasn’t just a wife and mother to Beau and Matthew. She was my mom. She was our mom, and by extension, she’s all of her mom,” Culkin said.
“She may have forgotten me, twice,” Culkin said, poking fun at the movies’ plots, “but we will always remember her.”
Murphy, who with Levy played the adult kids of O’Hara’s character in “Schitt’s Creek,” said O’Hara’s laugh “challenged anyone who heard it to join in and be as delighted as she was.”
Levy said the most important lesson he learned from O’Hara was to “say yes” to new challenges and adventures, including the joyful creation of her quirky bewigged character Moira Rose.

“Say yes to her naming that wig,” Levy said. “Say yes to giving her space to experiment and create. It will amaze you on a daily basis, and it will change your life. Say yes to her dinner invites and her stories and her wisdom and her generosity.”

Later during the “In Memoriam” segment, Grammy-nominated singer-songwriter Noah Kahan performed Simon & Garfunkel’s hit 1970 ballad “Bridge Over Troubled Water” as viewers saw images of other beloved stars who died over the past year, including Dolly Parton, James Van Der Beek, Hayden Panettiere, Eric Dane and more.
On the red carpet before the ceremony, Kahan explained to TODAY’s Sheinelle Jones why he chose to sing “Bridge Over Troubled Water” for Parton and others.
“It’s always represented so much hope and peace and kindness, which I think Dolly personified throughout her life and career,” said Kahan.

“We lost so many legends this year. I am really excited to get the chance to help memorialize them and to pay the respect to those who have contribute to this amazing industry and to art and culture,” added the singer.
The “In Memoriam” segment ended with a tearful Jamie Lee Curtis honoring late creator and director James Burrow and Hollywood director Rob Reiner, who she called a “cherished legend.”
Reiner got his start in television as an actor on “All in the Family” in the 1970s. Curtis described Reiner as “generous and kind and funny as hell and a friend to all.”
Last week, Reiner won a posthumous Emmy for a guest role on “The Bear,” Curtis revealed, breaking a record his father, comedy giant Carl Reiner, had held for longest time in between Emmy wins.
Reiner’s last Emmy award for acting came 48 years ago for “All in the Family.”

title: Reba McEntire Honors Dolly Parton at 2026 Emmys With Touching Cover Performance
summary: Sally Field and Reba McEntire paid a special tribute to their late longtime friend Dolly Parton at the 2026 Emmys.
story: Sally Field and Reba McEntire paid a special tribute to their late longtime friend Dolly Parton at the 2026 Emmys.

“If there are truly angels on earth then we just lost one: Dolly Parton,” said Field, who co-starred alongside Parton, Julia Roberts, Shirley MacLaine, Olympia Dukakis and Daryl Hannah in the 1989 comedy “Steel Magnolias.”
“I adored her from day one and how could you not?” said Field. She remembered Parton, who died Aug. 25 at age 80 after a brief cancer battle, as “blisteringly funny.”
“She was genuine and humble and supportive,” Field said before acknowledging Parton’s humanitarianism had “made a profound difference” in the lives of many around the country.
“God bless you, Dolly Parton. I am not the only one on earth who will love you forever and forever,” Field said before footage of Parton appeared onscreen.
McEntire then took the stage to perform Parton’s ballad “Appalachian Memories.”
After Parton’s family announced her death, McEntire was among the first celebrities to pay tribute in an emotional Instagram post.
“There will never ever be another you,” McEntire wrote alongside a gallery of images of the longtime friends. “We will remember and cherish every memory and every note you ever played and sang.”
“She’s gonna have a blast in heaven singing all her favorite songs with all her family and friends who have gone on before her,” she added.
McEntire revealed during a “MasterClass” session on country music that she first met the Queen of Country in September 1977 backstage at the Grand Ole Opry in Nashville.
McEntire, who was scheduled to make her debut at the famed venue that night, learned the performance would be cut short because Parton, already a major star, had shown up unannounced.

“So I walked in, and they said, ‘Reba, I’m terribly sorry, but the two songs that we said you could sing, you’re only going to get to sing one. I said, ‘Why?’ And they said, ‘Well, Dolly Parton just pulled in the parking lot, and she’s going to take one of your songs.”
Rather than feel slighted, McEntire was thrilled.
“I said, ‘OK, can I meet her?!’” she recalled, laughing. “I didn’t care or anything. I just wanted to see Dolly Parton.”
McEntire also recalled seeing Parton for the first time backstage.
“She came walking in and I kind of backed up against the wall, and she had on the most beautiful black chiffon pantsuit with rhinestone butterflies on them and her beautiful hair,” McEntire said.
“I thought, ‘My gosh, that’s probably what an angel looks just like right there.”

title: Taylor Swift Attends Chiefs Season Opener Alongside Tom Cruise
summary: Find out if Taylor Swift attended the Chiefs vs Broncos game at Arrowhead Stadium on Sept. 14, 2026.
story: After a summer filled with love and celebration, Travis Kelce is switching his focus to the football field as his Kansas City Chiefs are set to take on the Denver Broncos in their opener to the 2026 NFL season.

The star tight end and Taylor Swift tied the knot in July at Madison Square Garden, surrounded by their family and A-list friends. Since then, Travis Kelce has been sharing a few details about the nuptials, in between discussing his hopes for the Chiefs’ season with brother Jason Kelce on their “New Heights” podcast. Now that football is officially back, the newlywed, who is entering his 14th season, is looking toward his team’s championship aspirations.
Throughout the season, he’ll likely have his bride cheering him on from the stands, where she has been frequently spotted at both home and away games since the two started dating in 2023.

The pop icon made an appearance at the season opener on Sept. 14, marking her return to Arrowhead Stadium since saying “I do”. She was photographed celebrating multiple touchdowns with Tom Cruise by her side.
Here’s what we know about the game and Swift’s attendance.
When Do the Chiefs and Broncos Play?
The Kansas City Chiefs will kick off their 2026 NFL season against the Denver Broncos at Arrowhead Stadium on Monday, Sept. 14. It will be the last game of Week 1.
What Time Do the Chiefs and Broncos Play?
The game, which will see the teams go head to head for the first time since the Broncos defeated the Chiefs on Christmas Day last year, will begin at 5:15 p.m. PT/8:15 p.m. ET.
How to Watch and Stream the Chiefs-Broncos Game?
The game will air live simultaneously on ABC and ESPN. Fans who want to stream the game can watch via Disney+.
Was Taylor Swift at the Chiefs-Broncos Game?
Yes, Swift was spotted at the Sept. 14 game between the Chiefs and Broncos. She watched the matchup with Tom Cruise. The two hugged and high-fived when the Chiefs scored.

title: Taylor Swift Appears Alongside Mariska Hargitay in Emmys ‘SVU’ Sketch
summary: Mariska Hargitay seemingly used her pull as host of the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards to get friend and longtime “Law & Order: SVU” fan Taylor Swift to appear in a sketch about the show.
story: “Saccharide. Aries. From the vineyard. North or south.”

These arbitrary phrases have left Swifties everywhere with dozens of questions after the Emmy Awards, the main one being: Is Taylor Swift the mastermind her fans know her to be, or did she just send them on a wild goose chase?

Clues point to the former. But first, let’s rewind for those who need it: Mariska Hargitay had hosted the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards on Sept. 14 and had tapped Swift, her friend and longtime “Law & Order: SVU” fan, to appear in an “SVU” parody skit that aired during the telecast.
The pre-taped sketch features Hargitay, Ice-T, Kelli Giddish, Peter Scanavino and more actors playing their characters from the crime drama. Their case to crack: Will Taylor Swift attend the Emmys?

Hargitay, as Olivia Benson, brought up as evidence Swift’s love of Easter eggs. She wheeled out a crime board filled with clues as each person took turns suggesting why certain nominees and shows pointed toward Swift making a surprise appearance.
Suddenly, a crime board was wheeled away to reveal Swift was standing in the precinct.
“Hey guys, this isn’t adding up,” she said while wearing a gray suit and holding a coffee mug.
Ice-T rebuffed her input. “And who asked you, rookie?” he said.
She replied, “Our perp has a clear M.O. A lot of this doesn’t fit the pattern, and I don’t think everything is a clue.”
“It is to the Swifties,” Hargitay quickly replied.
“I think what we’re going to be looking for is hiding in plain sight,” Swift replied.
She then panned and spoke directly to the camera: “Saccharide. Aries. From the vineyard. North or south.”
“What did you just say?” Hargitay asked her.
“I didn’t say anything,” Swift said with a shrug.

While the sketch wraps by cracking its case — Swift won’t be at the Emmys because she’ll be busy supporting husband Travis Kelce at the Chiefs season opener — the meaning of Swift’s spoken message is still a mystery.
Swifties of course know that nothing is ever that simple when it comes to the singer. They immediately began dissecting the skit on social media, seeing if they could decode a secret message.
What could it mean? Well, the Emmys executive producers have confirmed that the words have some type of significance because they were specifically chosen by Swift.

After the Emmys, executive producers Jesse Collins, Dionne Harmon and Jeannae Rouzon-Clay from Jesse Collins Entertainment, and NBCUniversal live events and specials exec VP Jen Neal, spoke with reporters and explained how they pulled off the sketch.
“Taylor loved the script and she had some thoughts and we worked that in,” Collins told reporters, according to Variety.
One of Swift’s notes was to add Easter eggs, Collins revealed.
“She wanted them to be really official. And correct,” Rouzan-Clay shared.

As always, Swifties are on the case, and they might’ve already cracked it. Many shared their theories on social media that the sketch pointed to Swift releasing the long-awaited “Taylor’s Versions” from her debut and “Reputation” albums.
One Swiftie said on X that Ice-T’s “rookie” line and Aries, the first astrological sign, reference her self-titled first album.

Another zoomed in on the crime board and noticed a Post-it note that read “Is it TV?” adding more fuel to the fire. The board also had a heart similar to the one Swift used to draw on the back of her hand during the early days of her career.
Beneath the post, one X user replied, “Olivia said ‘the answer has been TV this whole time’ also.”
But others were more convinced that “Reputation (Taylor’s Version)” is on the way.

“I believe Debut TV is next but to add fuel to the Rep TV fire (no pun intended), if you go all the way back to the Karma MV in the Reputation scene Taylor wears the ram mask and the ram is the Aries zodiac animal,” one tweeted.
Over on Reddit, the speculation continued.
“I’m putting in my guess now — these are Rep vault track titles,” one suggested.
And one fan had a wild but plausible idea.
“OMG GUYS THERES TWO BOARDS!!! TWO!!” they said. “We are getting both Debut and Rep.”
Looks like we’ll have to wait for Swift’s next message to see what other tricks she has up her sleeve.
